**CMC research summary, Tuesday 2026-11-17, about 12:10 PM CT**

I found no news item explaining the November slide. The decline looks like drift after the October earnings, not a new event. New searches stopped turning up anything new after about seven queries and two page reads, but I found no November steel-sector data at all, so that gap is still open.

**The story**
- **Latest earnings (Oct 15, fiscal Q4, year ended Aug 31):**
  - Adjusted EPS was $2.09 against about $1.96 expected. Revenue was $2.66B, up 25.7%, also a beat.
  - Core EBITDA was $393.7M, up 35.1%. For the full year it was about $1.4B, up from $837M.
  - The stock barely moved on the report (about -0.5%).
- **North America Steel (the core business):**
  - Adjusted EBITDA was $317.5M, up 32.6%. Metal margin was $652/ton, up $42 from the prior quarter.
  - Management cited momentum in rebar and merchant bar pricing. Merchant bar shipments rose 27.5%, helped by data center demand and the Arizona 2 micro mill.
  - Downstream backlog was up 15.5% year over year.
- **Weak spots:**
  - Precast (residential-exposed, Southeast soft) came in below management's targets. Precast adjusted EBITDA was $57.0M.
  - An unplanned outage at the Galvabar plant hurt reinforcing-steel shipments. A second line is due later in 2026.
  - Europe Steel EBITDA fell to $15.6M from $39.1M, because the prior year had a $30.7M CO2 credit.
  - One source says the quarter's strength came almost entirely from the legacy steel business.
- **Next quarter's outlook:**
  - North America Steel EBITDA is expected to be nearly flat, with better pricing offset by higher scrap, startup costs and seasonal volume.
  - Construction Solutions is expected to fall seasonally. Europe should rise meaningfully, helped by a CO2 credit.
  - There is no numeric full-year guide. Management expects "another strong year."
  - The flat guide with seasonal softness is a plausible reason for the post-earnings drift lower.
- **Capital and balance sheet:**
  - Leverage is 1.9x and liquidity is over $2B. Fiscal 2026 capex was $580M and acquisitions were $2.5B, mostly precast.
  - The board added $600M to the buyback, and $702M was available at quarter end. Only $26.7M was bought in the quarter, so the buyback is a possible support but has been used lightly.
  - The dividend is $0.20 a quarter and was paid Nov 11. The ex-dividend date was Oct 28, so it is not a factor now.
- **Management:** The CFO retires Jan 15, 2027. Kenji Hashimoto is deputy CFO and the successor.
- **Analysts (MarketBeat):**
  - Consensus is "Moderate Buy" (10 buy, 4 hold, 1 sell) with an average target of $78.73.
  - After earnings, BMO cut its target to $73 (market perform) and Morgan Stanley cut to $84 (overweight). Barclays raised to $77 (equal weight). Goldman reiterated Buy at $85 in August.
  - The targets sit about 25-35% above the price, which is no catalyst by itself.
- **Valuation and technicals:**
  - P/E is about 11 and beta 1.55. The article puts the 52-week range at $57.01 to $84.87, against your 56.33 low, so the data sources differ slightly.
  - MarketBeat's 50-day ($65.00) and 200-day ($68.76) are close to your figures.
  - The stock was about $62 on Nov 12-13 and is now 59.27. Price is drifting toward the 52-week low, on elevated volume with no news.
- **Industry backdrop:**
  - The 50% Section 232 steel tariffs still support domestic pricing, and US sheet prices had their sharpest move in nearly 20 months in early November.
  - Data center construction is the one strong rebar and merchant-bar demand driver. Other construction is weak.
  - Nucor reported record shipments in Q2 2026, but sector stock performance has been mixed.
  - I found no US rebar price or scrap data for November 2026. The snippets I found were mostly from 2025 or from Turkey and Asia, where scrap and rebar firmed slightly in early November.

**For the trade decision**
- **Bearish:**
  - The stock is in a clean downtrend, below falling 50-day and 200-day averages, and breaking its 20-day low.
  - Guidance is flat, precast is weak, and the cycle is mature.
  - Beta is high, and a new 52-week low is plausible.
- **Bullish:**
  - Earnings were strong and valuation is low (about 11x earnings).
  - Analyst targets and the buyback authorization sit well above the price.
  - There is no negative news behind the drop, so it may be sector or flow selling.
  - The 52-week low (56.33 on your screen) is about 5% below the price.
- **Catalysts in the next 1-10 sessions:** none known. Earnings are not until Jan 7, and the CFO transition is Jan 15. I could not verify any sector news or macro driver for the last two weeks.

**Genomics and diagnostics basket: research as of 12:10 PM CT, Tuesday 2026-11-17**

**Bottom line.** I found no single sector event behind the basket's 20-day slide. It is a set of earnings-driven drops plus a rough tape for cancer-test names, and the drops are not uniform. NTRA, GH and TWST sold off on their own reports. TEM and ADPT reported well and the market reaction was mixed or unclear. NEO barely moved. I found nothing that explains NTRA's -2.9% today. Several price figures conflict across sources, so check live quotes before sizing anything.

**Natera (NTRA), the main drag**
- Q3 was reported Nov 5.
  - Revenue was $794M, up 34%, a beat. Excluding revenue true-ups, growth was 42%.
  - The EPS loss was $0.42 against about $0.27 expected.
  - Guidance was raised to $3.005–3.035B from $2.85–2.91B. Gross margin guidance of 64–66% was kept.
  - The top of the SG&A range was raised to $1.3B, and R&D was also raised. Management plans 2027 opex growth of 10–12%.
  - Clinical MRD volume (Signatera, the tumor-recurrence test) grew 56%. Signatera's average selling price is about $1,290.
- CEO Steve Chapman stepped down immediately. Solomon Moshkevich, the 15-year insider who ran clinical diagnostics, replaced him. Chapman stays on as consultant and board advisor.
- The new CEO set a $6B revenue target for 2029.
- The stock fell about 14–15% on Nov 6, its largest one-day drop in over a year. It had already fallen on Nov 2 (about -8.5%, with no company news) and Nov 5.
- Weiss says the stock is about 32% below its Oct 6 high of $437.41.
- Sources report different Nov 16 moves, between -6% and -9.6%. A MarketBeat item has it trading at $279.48 today.
- Analysts have not capitulated, but targets were trimmed.
  - JPMorgan cut to $405 and Baird to $403, both keeping bullish ratings.
  - Canaccord kept Buy with a $500 target.
  - Piper reiterated Overweight at $363.50.
  - Consensus target is about $394.
- A director sold about $1M of stock after the earnings report.
- Pending items:
  - The FIND colorectal screening study has finished enrolling 30,000 patients, with a readout in 2027.
  - Natera is appealing a $292.5M false-advertising verdict in favor of Guardant.
  - Medicare coverage decisions on more Signatera uses are pending.
  - Japan reimbursement news is expected around the JPMorgan Healthcare Conference in January.

**Guardant Health (GH)**
- Q3 revenue was $361M, up 36%, about 3% above consensus. Adjusted EPS was -$0.29 against -$0.31 expected. Free cash flow was about -$37M, an improvement. The full-year revenue guide was raised only slightly, to about $1.37B at the midpoint.
- The stock fell about 10% on Nov 5 to about $137.56. The article gave no cause beyond "the market hoped for more."
- Guardant priced a $500M 0% convertible due 2032 on Nov 12.
  - Most of the proceeds are earmarked to buy back about $395M of its 2027 converts and pay $51.7M for capped calls.
  - This is largely a refinancing, but the announcement is a common reason for a stock to dip.
- GH fell about 5% on Nov 16 to about $144. It traded in a $141–149 range today. Piper cut its target from $193 to $190.

**Tempus AI (TEM)**
- Q3 was reported Nov 2.
  - Revenue was $411.5M, up 23%.
  - The GAAP net loss narrowed to $14.9M from $80M.
  - Adjusted EBITDA was $25.6M, its first positive adjusted quarter on some measures.
  - Full-year revenue guidance is $1.60–1.605B, and cash is $854M.
- The stock reaction is murky, because sources conflict. One shows a +11% close on Nov 9 at $76.05. Another shows $75.89 as of Nov 12. I could not find today's price.
- The $1.5B Personalis acquisition cleared regulatory review. Personalis shareholders vote Nov 30.
- H.C. Wainwright raised its target to $85, and BTIG's target is $100.
- TEM looks like the strongest name in the basket, not a broken one.

**Adaptive Biotechnologies (ADPT)**
- Q3 was reported Nov 4, with the call on Nov 5.
  - MRD (clonoSEQ) revenue was $72.6M, up 28%.
  - Test volume was 39,587, up 46%.
  - It posted its first company-wide profit.
  - MRD guidance was raised to $276–286M.
  - Total revenue fell 11% because the Genentech comparison was one-time.
  - Immune Medicine revenue fell 70%.
- A separation of the Immune Medicine business is being worked on with Morgan Stanley, and management will update by year-end. That is a possible catalyst inside or after your window.
- I could not find a clean earnings-day price move. One snapshot shows $28.70 on Nov 6.

**NeoGenomics (NEO)**
- Q3 was reported Oct 28.
  - Revenue was $209M, up 11%.
  - Adjusted EBITDA was $19M.
  - NGS revenue grew 29%.
  - Guidance was raised: revenue $807–809M, adjusted EBITDA about $60M.
  - COO Warren Stone becomes CEO on Jan 4, 2027.
- The stock was about $17.9 and flat on the news.
- NEO is the slow, low-drama name in the group.

**Twist Bioscience (TWST)**
- Fiscal Q4 was reported Nov 12.
  - Revenue was a record $126.6M, up 28%.
  - Adjusted EBITDA was positive for the first time, at $2.2M.
  - The fiscal 2027 guide is $550–560M, about 21% growth. Gross margin guidance is about 52.5–53%, roughly flat.
  - Revenue from AI drug-discovery customers rose 175% to $59.1M, with about $100M expected next year. Management admitted "some concentration" in that customer base.
- The stock fell about 19% to about $98.87 from $122.59, despite the beat. That points to a growth or margin expectation reset.
- TWST is the only name in the basket that is not a clinical test company. It is an AI-and-biotech tools story, so it can move apart from the others.

**Sector and market context**
- On Nov 2, Natera's peers also fell: Myriad -7.9%, Guardant -4.5%, with Illumina, Labcorp and Quest down less. That fits some group-wide pressure.
- GRAIL reported Nov 4. Revenue was $37.5M against about $45.3M expected, and the stock fell sharply. An FDA decision on its Galleri test is expected by early Q1 2027. This weighed on the blood-cancer-test group around Nov 5–6.
- CMS released the CRUSH anti-fraud proposed rule on Nov 16. Analysts see minimal direct impact on diagnostics. One Seeking Alpha piece says some diagnostic stocks gained on it, but I could not read that article (it was blocked). Comments run through January 2027, so it is not a near-term driver.
- I found no news of lab reimbursement cuts or an FDA lab-test rule driving the group.

**What this means for a 1–10 session trade**
- The basket's -14% over 20 days is mostly NTRA (about -27% in a month), TWST (-19% on one day) and GH (about -10% plus the convert). TEM and NEO are holding up. One of six names is above its 50-day average.
- The drop was set off by identifiable events, and the fundamentals (growth, guidance raises, tightening losses) did not worsen. That makes this a sentiment and positioning reset, not a thesis break, for NTRA, GH and TWST.
- Against that, the damage came from insider-heavy and leadership news (the NTRA CEO exit, the director's sale) and from guidance expectations. Nothing has yet marked an end to the selling.
- There is no scheduled catalyst for most of the names before Nov 30. The exceptions are the Personalis vote for TEM on Nov 30 and the ADPT separation update by year-end.
- NTRA is making new lows on continued selling, so a bounce is not yet established. TWST is the cleanest "overreaction on a beat" candidate. TEM and NEO are not the oversold pieces.

I found no company-specific news that explains the drop. The decline looks like a broad software/AI-infrastructure selloff ahead of earnings. I could not open several sources (GuruFocus, MarketBeat, AlphaStreet all returned 403), so some points rest on search snippets. Treat those as lower confidence.

**What the business is**
- Nutanix sells hybrid-cloud and hyperconverged infrastructure software. It is a main beneficiary of customers leaving VMware after Broadcom's takeover.
- At its .NEXT conference in April 2026, the CEO said about 30,000 customers have left VMware. Analysts describe the exit as slow, with customers moving at renewal time.
- Growth areas now are external storage (the largest growth contributor expected for FY27), neoclouds, and agentic AI. New or expanded partnerships in FY26 include Dell, AMD, Lenovo, NetApp, Nvidia and Netris.

**Last report (Q4 FY26, Aug 26) was a beat, and the stock rose 6% or more after hours**
- Revenue was $757.1M, up 16%, against a $738M consensus. Adjusted EPS was $0.60 against $0.49 expected.
- Annual recurring revenue (ARR) was $2.55B, up 16%. Free cash flow was $277.6M. Adjusted operating margin was 26.2%.
- FY26 revenue was $2.85B, up 12%. Total contract value booked grew in the high teens.
- The company added 650 customers in the quarter, for 32,360 total.
- It cut about 5% of the workforce, roughly 400 jobs, substantially done by the end of October. Restructuring costs are about $33–43M, with about $30–35M paid in cash in Q1.

**Guidance, which is the key setup for the print**
- Q1 FY27 (reported Nov 24): revenue of $755–765M and a non-GAAP operating margin of 26–28%. Consensus is about $762M in revenue and about $0.61 in EPS (MarketBeat). Another source shows $0.53.
- FY27: revenue of $3.18–3.23B, a 24–25% adjusted operating margin, and free cash flow of $850–950M.
- The FY27 guide implies about 12% growth, flat against FY26. It assumes server supply constraints and hardware price rises continue.
- The CEO said "we don't see any near-term letup" in hardware price increases. Software prices are unchanged, but some licenses start later to match delayed server deliveries.
- The FY27 free cash flow margin is guided slightly lower, at about 28% against 29%. Nutanix is moving to annual payments and third-party financing.
- An analyst (Jason Ader) called the guide conservative. Nutanix has beaten its own guide before, which is the usual bull argument.

**AAOI research summary, 12:10 PM CT, Tue 2026-11-17**

I did not find a single clean cause for the slide. Several pieces overlap: sector-wide AI-spending fear, a Q4 revenue guide that missed consensus, and a second China-policy headline that faded by midday. The fundamentals are strong but come with heavy dilution and customer concentration. Some of the search tool's summaries conflicted with each other, so I flag where a number rests on a single source. I did not get a verified primary source for the AI-funding-fear framing (the Stocktwits piece is undated).

**The story**
- **Business:** AAOI makes optical transceivers (800G and 1.6T) for AI datacenters, plus CATV gear. Q3 revenue was a record $269.9M, up about 128% year over year. Datacenter revenue was $155.6M versus $43.9M a year earlier. GAAP net income was $6.3M and non-GAAP EPS was $0.17 against $0.14 expected. Non-GAAP gross margin was 28.7%, below the 29–30.5% guide.
- **Q4 guide (given Nov 5):** Revenue of $385–420M, below the $427M consensus even at the top end. Non-GAAP EPS is $0.48–0.63 and non-GAAP gross margin 29.5–31%. Management expects $270–300M from datacenter.
- **Supply is the constraint, not demand.** A key customer moved to 1.6T faster than expected and AAOI ran short of parts. It holds about $450M of 1.6T orders but can ship only $50–70M of them in Q4. The CFO said demand will exceed capacity through 2027.
- **Capacity targets:** The end-2026 target was cut to over 500k units a month from 650k, because Texas Phase 2 slipped about 7 months on power and construction. The end-2027 target was raised to over 1M. Texas Phase 1 is due to start in December.
- **Customer contract (October):** A Tier 1 hyperscaler agreed to buy at least 10% of its 1.6T needs from AAOI through May 2029. Management estimates $1–1.5B of revenue, but the contract is conditional on AAOI's ability to supply. Prices are fixed with built-in cuts, and the customer committed no capital.
- **Concentration:** The top 10 customers were 99% of Q2 revenue. One source ties Amazon to the company through a warrant arrangement. I could not confirm that.
- **Balance sheet:** Cash was $621M and debt about $189M. The company raised about $588M in an at-the-market stock sale that finished Oct 5, at an average of $105.36. Roughly $1B has been raised in 2026, so dilution is ongoing. Insider selling has been heavy, with 12-month sales of about $72M by one tracker. Short interest was about 12–13% of float in spring and summer.

**Bottom line:** Today's 6.4% drop looks like sector selling, not news about MNDY. The company-specific story is weak: growth is slowing, retention is falling, and management says stability is "a few quarters" away. The stock was already marked down on that. The setup is a sector-driven flush into a long-term downtrend with no turn yet.

**Why it's down today**
- I found nothing MNDY-specific today.
- Software is being hit broadly. One report has the S&P 500 software and services index down 7.1%, a three-month low. Salesforce fell about 8–10%, ServiceNow 7%, MongoDB 7%, Intuit 7% and Datadog 5%.
- Reported drivers are money rotating out of software ahead of the Anthropic IPO and Nvidia earnings after the close. The IPO is said to price Wednesday and trade Thursday under "ANT."
- One report said investors may be selling software to make room for the IPO.
- The older worry also persists that AI tools replace or let customers build their own versions of SaaS products.
- I could not find an MNDY quote or article for today. The 74.93 comes from your screen.
- Yahoo showed a 11/16 close of 80.05, up 2.6%. Today's drop therefore erases that bounce.
- One source (the Seeking Alpha snippet) showed 75.65 on 11/10, so today's price is back near the post-earnings low.

**Q3 results (Nov 9)**
- Revenue was $377.5M, up 19% and above the company's $368–370M guide.
- Non-GAAP operating margin was a record 24% (vs 15% a year earlier).
- Q4 revenue guide is $380–382M, about 14% growth, against a consensus of about $385.7M. That is a sharp slowdown from 19%.
- Full-year 2026 guide is $1.473–1.475B (about 20% growth), with non-GAAP operating income of $268–270M.
- Adjusted free cash flow was $63M versus $92M a year earlier. The full-year adjusted FCF guide is $282–288M.
- Net dollar retention (NDR) fell to 108% (109% last quarter, 110% before that). Management expects the year to end at 107% and said to expect "some short-term modest pressure."
- Paid customers with more than 10 users grew only 5%. Larger accounts are healthier: customers over $50K ARR grew 26%, over $100K grew 33%, and over $500K grew 58%.
- AI ARR is $36M. Remaining performance obligations (contracted revenue not yet recognized) are $946M, up 27%.
- Cash plus securities is about $1.1B, down from about $1.5B of cash at the end of 2025. The company repurchased $735M of stock in the first nine months and none in Q3.

**What management said was wrong (call, per the Motley Fool transcript)**
- The July restructuring cut about 20% of staff (690 fewer heads in Q3) and caused disruption.
- Small-business customer adds fell and logo churn rose. Management calls this "by design" as it moves toward larger customers.
- Buyers are slower and more deliberate because they are weighing how AI fits their business.
- Customers find software through AI channels instead of traditional search, which adds volatility at the top of the funnel. A test shifting about 25% of marketing budget to agentic acquisition "didn't convert as much as we wished."
- Management expects stability "throughout 2027." Formal 2027 guidance comes with Q4 results, and next earnings are 2027-02-08.
- A new service, Frontier, may pressure margins.
- Analysts pressed on slowing net adds, weak cash flow and whether the restructuring disruption is over. Management said some large deals slipped to quarter-end.

Search snippets and aggregators also conflicted on prices and dates, so treat the figures below as approximate. My last round of searches turned up little new beyond the Iran-deal timing gap, but I didn't open every primary source. I never reached FedEx's own 8-K, and the Investor Day agenda and the Amazon glide-down details are also missing.

## The story
The basket is running on an air and ocean freight squeeze, tariff and customs work, and fuel surcharges. A US-Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz disruption sent diesel to records above $6 a gallon, so carriers have been collecting high surcharges. The stretch is uneven across the four names, and the news since early November has been thin.

## Per name

**Expeditors (EXPD)** is the strongest fundamental story.
- Q3 was reported Nov 3. EPS was $2.65 (up 62%) against about $2.23 expected, and revenue was $4.11B (up 42%).
- Airfreight tonnage grew 13%, accelerating from 8% in July to 19% in September. Management credited AI-infrastructure "hyperscaler" shipments and tight air capacity.
- Ocean volume grew 7% on Asian port congestion, which management expects to last through the rest of 2026. Customs brokerage revenue rose 29%.
- The stock hit an all-time high of about $200 on Oct 16, before earnings. It rose about 1.9% on earnings day.
- **Investor Day is tomorrow (Nov 18) morning in New York.** It is a binary event for the basket's strongest name. Consensus is roughly Hold, and the full-year EPS estimate is only about $7.65 to $7.84. UBS raised its target to $245.

**C.H. Robinson (CHRW)** is rallying inside a larger downtrend.
- CHRW agreed on Oct 5 to buy RXO for about $5.8B ($17.25 cash plus 0.0856 CHRW shares per RXO share). Management targets $300M in synergies, and the deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027. The stock fell about 10% on the announcement.
- Q3 was reported around Nov 3-4. Adjusted EPS was $1.80 against $1.75 expected. Adjusted gross profit rose 14.5% and truckload gross profit per load rose 17%. The stock still sold off on higher SG&A guidance, 2027 insurance inflation, softer freight demand and the deal. Reports of the move ranged from -2% to -9.6%.
- Buybacks are paused to protect the investment-grade rating. Operating cash flow was weak at $124M.
- It hit a 52-week low around Oct 30 (about $122-126) and was near $134.67 on Nov 16, against a high of $210 on Jul 22. So today's +1.9% is a bounce off lows.
- Truckload spot rates are up about 45-50% from a year ago, and capacity is tightening. Management expects spot rates to rise into the holidays. Insurance cost updates may come in an 8-K in mid-to-late December.

**UPS** is the beat-and-raise story, with a headwind from its shrinking Amazon volume.
- Q3 was reported Oct 27. Adjusted EPS was $1.69 against $1.63 expected, and revenue was $22.85B. Full-year guidance was raised to about $92.6B revenue and adjusted EPS of about $7.28.
- The stock rose about 5% to about $105 that day. It was up about 23% from Oct 6 to Nov 4.
- Analyst targets are mostly $114-135, with Barclays at $95 (Underweight). The average is about $115.
- The $1.64 dividend went ex on Nov 16, a mechanical drop of about 1.5%.
- Risks: it is cutting lower-margin volume from its largest customer, which will weigh on shipment comparisons for several more quarters. Holiday-quarter volume is expected below a year earlier. Supply chain profit fell, with a goodwill impairment.

**FedEx (FDX)** is the day's laggard.
- FedEx Freight was spun off on Jun 1 (ticker FDXF).
- The fiscal Q1 report came Oct 28. Adjusted EPS was $3.74 against about $3.32 expected, and revenue was about $22.9B (up 12%). Guidance was raised, with one summary giving $18.00-$18.60. The stock still fell after hours to about $301.
- It has since recovered to about $324 (Nov 12, up 1.5%). Its 52-week high is about $345.
- A new CFO, Jamere Jackson, starts Nov 30.
- The next earnings report is in mid-December (my inference, not confirmed). Today's -2.4% has no identified cause, though FDX looks to be giving back part of its rebound from about $301.

## Macro backdrop
- Diesel was $5.94 for the week ending Nov 16, down 19 cents in a week from a $6.29 peak around Nov 2. Parcel fuel surcharges lag diesel by one to two weeks.
- If diesel keeps falling, parcel carriers' surcharge revenue shrinks and the fuel-driven part of the story fades. A US-Iran deal, tentative or finalized, is the swing factor. I couldn't confirm what has happened this week.

## For a one-to-ten-session decision
- **Why the stretch:** UPS and EXPD rallied on earnings, and the basket is 2.0 standard deviations above its 50-day norm. The only visible rollover so far is FDX.
- **Mean-reversion argument:** The news flow is largely priced in (UPS at about 105 against a $115 average target, EXPD near its high). Falling diesel is a slow headwind to surcharge revenue, and CHRW's and FDX's moves look like noise.
- **Continuation argument:** Spot rates are rising into the holidays. EXPD's air and ocean strength is accelerating, and Investor Day could add a catalyst.
- **Dated events:** EXPD Investor Day on Nov 18, weekly diesel prints on Mondays, CHRW's insurance update in mid-to-late December, and FedEx's earnings in mid-December.
- **Diesel could hurt:** A sharp Iran-related oil drop would pressure the fuel-surcharge beneficiaries.

agents.report:
**HGV (Hilton Grand Vacations): research as of Tuesday 2026-11-17, midday**

**Summary:** HGV is a bad quarter that was sold hard, then bought back hard. The stock fell to about $35.71 into the Oct 29 print and is now about $45.57, roughly +28%. I found no new fundamental news behind the November leg. The likely drivers are a squeeze of heavy short interest, a $200M accelerated share repurchase (ASR) still running, and a "worst is behind us" read on sales. The risk is that the move is positioning rather than new information.

**What happened (Q3, reported Oct 29)**
- **Contract sales:** $807M, down 11% against guidance of a mid-single-digit decline. Value per guest (VPG) fell 12% to about $3,400. Tours rose 2% to 236K.
- **Guidance:** FY26 adjusted EBITDA was cut to $1.165–1.180B from about $1.225–1.265B.
- **Quality of the beat:** Headline EPS of $4.03 against a $1.08 consensus is not real. $296M ($3.76 per share) came from a one-time recognition on the Ka Haku (Hawaii) project. Adjusted EBITDA of $313M (+4%) was helped by a $55M loan-loss methodology change. The provision rate fell to 12.5% from 16.8%. Management said it should settle in the mid-teens, so this tailwind fades. Analysts pushed on this and management conceded it flattered the quarter.
- **Management's explanation:** Execution, not demand. Closing rates were weak, sales-force turnover was high, and incentives were misaligned. Orlando and Myrtle Beach (Bluegreen) were the worst, with new leaders installed. Sales and marketing cost was 51% of contract sales, up 440 bps. Comp-plan changes keep that rate higher in the short term.
- **Positives:**
  - Financing revenue rose 16%. HGV Max membership passed 300K.
  - Delinquencies are at a five-year low at Diamond and back to 2022 levels at Bluegreen.
  - Inventory spend was cut by $90M to about $285M.
  - Adjusted free cash flow was $63M.
- **Turnaround claim:** August was the low point. Several key sales centers returned to growth in September, and management said October continued that trend, with no figure given. Q4 guide: contract sales down low-to-mid single digits, VPG down mid-single digits. The sales force has added over 430 experienced reps.
- **2027:** Management called its long-term algorithm "achievable" and cited low-to-mid single-digit tour growth and low single-digit VPG growth. It said no M&A is in view.
- **Balance sheet:** Net leverage is 3.87x, with $4.9B corporate debt at 5.75%, of which about $2.9B is nonrecourse. Liquidity is $684M. Two Q4 securitizations are planned (Japan, and about $450–500M domestic). That is a possible near-term catalyst and funding signal.

**Capital return**
- The $600M FY26 buyback target was reaffirmed. Q3 buybacks were only $110M, below the $150M pace.
- On Oct 30, HGV signed a $200M ASR with Deutsche Bank. The initial delivery was about 4.48M shares, priced off the Oct 29 close of $35.71. It settles by Dec 31, with $417M of authorization remaining afterward.
- The dealer buys shares in the market over the term. That is a steady, price-insensitive bid for six weeks.

**Positioning and flow**
- Short interest was 13.9M shares as of Oct 30, up 82% in two weeks. That is about 19% of float and 11.2 days to cover. A squeeze fits the 25.9% 20-day gain. I did not find the Nov 15 figure.
- Insider activity:
  - CEO Mark Wang bought 12,200 shares at $40.92 on Nov 2 (about $499K).
  - Director Charles Corbin Jr. sold 60,401 shares at $43.41 on Nov 4 (about $2.6M). It was under a pre-arranged 10b5-1 plan.
- Institutions own about 97%. Beta is 1.6. Market cap is about $3.3B and trailing P/E about 6.5, which is inflated by the one-off.

**Analysts**
- Consensus is Hold: 2 Buy, 10 Hold, 1 Sell, with an average target of about $49.
- Citigroup and Citizens JMP both downgraded to market perform on Nov 2, according to MarketBeat. I could not corroborate Citi's move elsewhere.
- Barclays cut its target to $39 from $46. JPMorgan cut to $38 (neutral). Mizuho cut to $60 from $74.
- The stock is above the most recent targets from Barclays and JPMorgan. Targets are lagging price, so there is no analyst-driven upside catalyst.

**Peers and sector**
- Marriott Vacations (VAC) reported on Nov 4. Contract sales rose 29% and VPG rose 30%. It raised guidance, but cut its free cash flow guidance and raised its sales reserve. That shows industry demand is intact, which supports management's "company-specific execution" story. I could not confirm how VAC's stock reacted.
- Benzinga showed VAC near its yearly low around Nov 14, so I found no sector rally.
- Hilton Worldwide (HLT) fell 4.3% after its Q3 report.

**Price context**
- 52-week range is $33.99–$55.40. The 50-day average is about $37.8–37.9 and the 200-day about $44.5, which the stock just reclaimed.
- Near-term resistance is the 20-day high of $45.77, then the mid-$40s to $50 gap area.
- HGV sponsors the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix on Nov 19–21. That is marketing only.

**Read for a 1–10 session trade**
- **Bullish:** short covering and ASR bid continue, October and November sales trends confirm a turnaround, the Q4 securitizations price well, and a breakout through $45.77.
- **Bearish:**
  - RSI 74 and 3.0 ATR above the 20-day average are stretched. Volume on today's move is only about half normal, so there is no fresh buying.
  - Fundamentals are unchanged to weaker, the EBITDA guide was cut, and there is a provision-driven earnings-quality problem.
  - Analysts are neutral to negative and targets sit below price.
  - After a squeeze, shorts that have covered leave no fuel.
  - Insiders sold into the rally.
- **Biggest unknowns:** I found no reported catalyst for Nov 2–13, no up-to-date short interest, and no real-time October sales numbers. I found no scheduled company event in the next 10 sessions other than the securitizations and any 8-K or investor conference. The next earnings report is about February.

**Source caveats:** Webull and Simply Wall St (Oct 30) cited $38.45 for the post-earnings close and some revenue figures that don't match the 8-K. The 8-K says $1.961B revenue. Figures cited here come from the 8-K, the Fool and MarketBeat transcripts, and MarketBeat's Nov 15 short-interest article.

**Bottom line:** Today's move is most likely a deal-rumor spike. The only source I found for the catalyst is one unconfirmed Financial Times report that TPG is nearing a take-private of BILL. No price has been reported.

**Today's catalyst**
- Investing.com ([article](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/bill-holdings-shares-surge-on-reports-of-looming-tpg-takeprivate-deal-5033616)) was published Nov 17 at 11:46 AM, time zone not stated. It attributes the news to the FT, citing sources familiar with the matter.
- The report says TPG is nearing an agreement to take BILL private at a premium to its market value. No price per share or other terms were given.
- The deal is expected to be finalized "in the coming days." Insiders said the timeline is fluid and talks could collapse.
- TPG declined to comment, and BILL had not responded.
- A Seeking Alpha item on [TradingView](https://tradingview.com/news/seekingalpha:80846a735094b:0-bill-holdings-jumps-after-report-that-tpg-nearing-a-takeover) says the same, with a 7.9% move.
- I could not find the FT article itself, a second outlet confirming it, or any analyst reaction. Everything traces back to the FT.
- Both articles cite a market cap of about $4.8B, which looks stale next to a stock near $63.

**The sale backdrop**
- In Nov 2025 Bloomberg reported that BILL, under pressure from activist Starboard, was [exploring a sale](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-11-11/business-payments-firm-bill-holdings-is-exploring-a-sale).
- Elliott took a stake of at least 5% ([TipRanks](https://www.tipranks.com/news/bill-holdings-stock-bill-jumps-as-activist-elliott-builds-stake)). Barington took a stake and [pushed for a sale](https://www.hedgeweek.com/barington-takes-stake-in-bill-holdings-and-pushes-for-sale/). Starboard got two board seats in October.
- On Feb 6, 2026 Bloomberg reported that Hellman & Friedman held talks to buy BILL ([Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4548671-bill-holdings-surges-on-report-hellman-friedman-in-talks-to-buy)). The stock jumped about 37% to 40% that day, to roughly $49 to $50.
- Truist put takeout value at $59 to $70 a share in a Feb 6 note. That is an estimate, not an offer.
- I found nothing on how the H&F talks ended. That is a gap. The stock later fell back below $50, since the 200-day average is $43, so the earlier rumor did not become a deal.

**Fundamentals**
- Fiscal Q1 2027 was reported Nov 5 ([press release](https://www.bill.com/press-release/bill-reports-first-quarter-fiscal-year-2027-financial-results)).
- Core revenue was $316.4M, up 14%. Non-GAAP operating income was $136.9M, up 101%.
- Non-GAAP EPS was $1.18, about $0.20 above estimates.
- GAAP net income was $60.3M, and total payment volume was $102B, up 14%.
- BILL bought back about 7M shares for about $305M in the quarter.
- Revenue is now reported net of card rewards, which makes the headline total look weaker than earlier estimates.
- The count of businesses served fell again year over year, for the third quarter in a row (per [247wallst](https://247wallst.com/cards/bill-holdings-q1-2027-earnings-bill-01m6prkd65n8x09nv204h5bj3e), a third-party analysis).
- Fiscal Q2 guidance is core revenue growth of 10% to 13%. Management said Q1 expenses are not a new baseline.
- Headcount was cut by more than 30%.

**Run-up before today**
- On Nov 16, William Blair upgraded BILL to Outperform and the stock rose 5% to 9% to a new 52-week high near $58.35 ([Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-bill-holdings-stock-surging-today-93CH-5030571)). SPY was also down that day.
- Oppenheimer raised its target to $60. UBS initiated at Buy with a $64 target.
- The 17% gain over five sessions comes from the post-earnings drift, the upgrade and today's rumor combined.
- A midday [247wallst item](https://247wallst.com/cards/bill-holdings-bill-price-swing-01m7n79qkqs88kf2p1fry5za1k) called today's move "no clear catalyst" before the FT news spread.

**What this means for a 1 to 10 session trade**
- The outcomes are binary. A signed deal at a premium to a price already near $63 could add something, but the premium is unknown. Talks collapsing, or a deal priced near or below the market, would likely drop the stock sharply.
- The upside from here is capped by a deal price that may be close to where the stock trades. The downside is a fall back toward $55 to $58, or lower, if talks fail.
- Analyst targets of $60 to $64 and the Truist range of $59 to $70 are about where the stock now trades.
- The stock is extended, with RSI 83 and 7.6 times normal volume. A trade should treat it as event-driven. Check for a confirming announcement or a denial before sizing.
- The next earnings date, 2027-02-04, is irrelevant to this window.

agents.report:
**CRM, 12:10 PM CT, Tue 2026-11-17: research report**

**Bottom line:** CRM has no company-specific news today. The drop comes from three outside pressures: Anthropic's IPO, a broad market and sector selloff, and long-running doubts about AI disruption and acquisition spending. These came from about 15 searches and 9 page reads. The last few rounds turned up nothing new on today's cause. The Anthropic IPO is the one dated catalyst before earnings.

**Today's move**
- Monday's close was $214.83. Reports put CRM at $194.09 to $197.29 midday, down about 8% to 9.7%. It was the Dow's worst performer.
- The broad market was weak. Investing.com showed the S&P 500 down 1.15%, the Nasdaq down 1.11% and the VIX at 26, up 13%.
- Peers fell with it. Yahoo reported HubSpot and ServiceNow down about 7% and Workday down about 5%. That makes this sector-wide, not CRM-specific.
- A Korean outlet (JKN) reported a close of $201.03, down 6.4%. It does not match the other reports, so I'd ignore it.

**Why it fell (reported explanations)**
1. **Anthropic IPO, the main one.**
   - Anthropic is reported to price its IPO Wednesday 11/18 and trade on Nasdaq as ANT on Thursday 11/19. The raise is reported as up to about $64B.
   - The Yahoo article's theory is that funds are selling seat-priced software to raise cash for the offering.
   - RBC's Rishi Jaluria warned that "the AI companies are going to try to destroy Salesforce entirely."
   - A Trefis piece on 11/12, citing CNBC, put Anthropic's fully diluted value at $1.26T to $1.41T. That is about 2.5 times the combined value of CRM, NOW, ADBE, INTU and WDAY. Only one source gave this price range.
   - The core fear is that AI agents reduce the number of seats Salesforce can sell.
   - The market has had this fear since the February 2026 "SaaSpocalypse" selloff, which was set off by Claude Cowork and its plug-ins.
2. **Doubts about Agentforce and AI spending.** Investing.com says IT buyers are delaying deployments, but its "channel checks" claim has no cited source and the article was AI-assisted. IBTimes says investors doubt how fast Agentforce will turn into revenue.
3. **Acquisitions.** All three deals below are cash or debt-funded, and buybacks have not reduced the share count.
   - Braze, announced 10/20: $5.66B cash at $47.50 a share, about a 58% premium, expected to close in fiscal 2028 (starting February 2027). CRM fell only 1% to 3% on that news.
   - Fin (formerly Intercom): $3.6B, announced in June and still pending.
   - Contentful: completed 9/1.
4. **Optimizely breach mention (minor).** TipRanks says CRM was named in a report on Optimizely malicious code. My own search found only a February 2026 Optimizely voice-phishing breach, in which Salesforce was a customer and not compromised. I'd treat this as noise.
5. **Technical breakdown.** The stock broke support and momentum turned bearish, which fits your screen.

**Background**
- **Last earnings (8/26, fiscal Q2 2027):**
  - The stock jumped about 13% after hours to roughly $232, its biggest post-earnings gain since August 2024. A few outlets reported larger moves.
  - Agentforce ARR passed $1.5B, up more than 240%. The company changed the definition to include more products, so it is not directly comparable with earlier figures.
  - Revenue was $11.3B, up 11%, including $456M from Informatica. Organic growth was only about 6%.
  - Current remaining performance obligation (cRPO, contracted future revenue) was $33.5B, up 14%.
  - FY27 revenue guidance was raised to $46.1B to $46.4B. Of the raise, only $100M was organic; the rest came from acquisitions, less a currency drag.
  - Management said it is on track for "second-half organic revenue reacceleration" and Benioff declared the SaaSpocalypse over.
  - Q3 revenue guidance is $11.42B to $11.5B, with cRPO growth of about 14%, excluding Contentful and Fin.
- **Quality of that beat:** adjusted EPS was $5.90, but SaaStr and Zacks say it came largely from a mark-up on Salesforce's Anthropic stake plus the buyback. Yahoo says the stake was about 45% of a $11.3B strategic investment portfolio as of 7/31.
- **Buyback:** a $25B accelerated share repurchase, targeting at least 14% of shares at about $176 average cost, with settlement expected in October. Today's price is about 10% above that average.
- **The stock before today:** CRM was about $232 after the August earnings and $214.83 on Monday. It is down roughly 19% to 25% year to date and about 28% from the 52-week high of about $269.
- **Earlier analyst downgrades:**
  - Morgan Stanley moved to Equal Weight on about 7/21, with a $185 target.
  - KeyBanc moved to Sector Weight on 7/9.
  - Bank of America reinstated coverage at Underperform with a $160 target on 5/18.
  - I found none in November.
- **Current analyst view:** consensus is Strong Buy. TipRanks puts the average target at about $281 and shows 30 Buy and 9 Hold ratings. Stifel reiterated Buy with a $300 target on 11/16, and Piper Sandler ($280) and J.P. Morgan reiterated Buy.
- **Valuation:** the Yahoo article says forward P/E was about 15x before the drop, against a five-year average of about 27x. Trefis shows 4.1x price/sales. Consensus EPS estimates were unchanged.

**Upcoming dates**
- 11/18: Anthropic IPO prices.
- 11/19: Anthropic is expected to start trading as ANT.
- 11/24: Workday reports earnings, a read-through for CRM.
- 12/2: CRM earnings after the close. The Yahoo article says it needs organic growth above the prior quarter's 6% to counter the seat-count fears. That falls outside a 1 to 10 session window unless the hold runs to about 11 sessions.

**Read for a 1 to 10 session trade**
- **Bullish case:**
  - The sector is hit on flow-based selling, not a company change.
  - Estimates are unchanged.
  - The stock has just fallen below its 200-day average and into the $176 buyback cost area.
  - Sell-side targets are far above the price.
  - Pre-earnings drift and a bounce after the Anthropic IPO is done are possible.
- **Bearish case:**
  - The IPO is not priced until tomorrow, and ANT trading starts Thursday. Selling pressure could continue or intensify.
  - Market-wide risk-off (VIX 26) adds to it.
  - The AI-disruption story has repeatedly produced multi-day software selloffs.
  - Short-term momentum is clearly down.
- **What I could not verify:**
  - the exact closing price (reports range from about $194 to $201),
  - confirmation of the IPO timing from a primary source (it comes from Yahoo, TipRanks and Trefis, citing CNBC),
  - whether any new analyst actions followed today's drop.

I'm stopping here. The last few searches added little new, apart from the Nov 16 and Nov 17 quotes, which conflict.

## Bottom line
The basket weakness comes from sentiment and positioning, not broken fundamentals. Four of the six reported Q3 results that were mostly beats with raised guidance, and the stocks sold off anyway. I found no single catalyst for the last five sessions. Natera and Guardant both sold off around their Nov 5–6 reports and fell again on Nov 16 with no news that I could find.

## Names (all dates 2026)
- **Natera (NTRA):** This is the main driver.
  - Q3 revenue was $794M, up 34%, and 2026 guidance went to $3.005–3.035B from $2.85–2.91B. Clinical MRD units were about 316K, up 56%, and Signatera ASP was about $1,290.
  - The stock still fell 14–15% on Nov 6. The GAAP loss per share ($0.42) was wider than expected, and CEO Steve Chapman stepped down, with Solomon Moshkevich succeeding him.
  - It was at a 52-week high of $436 on Oct 29. After the Nov 6 drop, sources put it at about $289–299 on Nov 16, down 6–10% that day with no news. That is about 30% off the high.
  - Valuation was about 20x trailing sales before the drop. Insiders sold $365M over 12 months and bought nothing.
  - Roth cut its target to $405 from $475, and BTIG kept Buy with a $430 target. I found no downgrades.
  - Medicare coverage for transplant monitoring began Aug 30, and a Phase II collaboration with Incyte was announced Nov 10.
  - Management set a $6B revenue goal for 2029.
- **Guardant (GH):** Q3 revenue was $361M, up 36%. Shield screening volume was 83K tests, up 246%, and Shield cost per test fell to $330 from $410.
  - 2026 revenue guidance went to $1.36–1.37B. The stock fell about 12% after hours because free-cash-flow burn guidance rose to $205–220M from $195–205M.
  - Management attributes $10–15M of that to a temporary CMS claims delay for Guardant360 Liquid. The cash shifts into 2027.
  - GH was about $144 on Nov 16 after a 5% drop, near $171 on Nov 2, and had a 52-week high of $191. Analyst sentiment is overwhelmingly Buy.
- **Tempus (TEM):** This is the relative-strength name.
  - Q3 revenue was $411.5M, up 23%. Adjusted EBITDA was $25.6M, 2026 revenue guidance went to $1.60B, and the stock rose about 10% after the Nov 2 report.
  - The Personalis acquisition (about $1.5B, announced in July) caused a dilution selloff then. I did not confirm whether it has closed.
- **Adaptive (ADPT):** Q3 was its first profitable quarter, with adjusted EBITDA of $14.3M. clonoSEQ volume was about 39.6K tests, up 46%, and MRD guidance was raised.
  - The risk is CMS preliminary 2027 rates. Adaptive says the data behind its code is wrong and is trying to get it corrected, with final rates due around now (November). The prior rate was $2,007.
  - I found one quote of about $29.94, near the 52-week high of about $30.7. JPMorgan raised its target to $35 on Nov 6.
  - This is likely the basket member above its 50-day average, but I can't confirm that. The final CMS rate is a binary risk during your hold window.
- **NeoGenomics (NEO):** Q3 revenue was $209M, up 11%, and NGS revenue grew 29%. Management raised 2026 revenue guidance to $807–809M.
  - It expects reimbursement for two new RaDaR indications, one by year-end and one by mid-2027, per the Stephens conference on Nov 17.
  - One quote showed $15.08 on Nov 17, down 2%, against $16.84 on Nov 6. Consensus targets are about $21–23.
- **Twist (TWST):** Fiscal Q4 revenue was $126.6M, up 28%, with its first positive adjusted EBITDA (+$2.2M). FY27 guidance is $550–560M, up about 21%.
  - The stock fell as much as 19% on Nov 12 from $122.59 to about $98.87, as investors focused on the outlook.
  - It was already down 15% on Nov 2 in a no-news genomics-tools slide. Today's +2.5% is a small bounce.

## Sector context
- On Nov 2, with no news, TXG fell 12%, TWST 15% and PacBio 10%, while NTRA fell 8.5%, Myriad 7.9% and GH 4.5%. XLV was down only 0.1%.
- Janus Henderson attributes the move to a tech and AI selloff after the midterms spreading into richly valued genomics and diagnostics names.
- GeneDx fell about 17% on Nov 10 on reimbursement concerns, adding to the group's weakness.
- I could not confirm any sector-wide news for Nov 13–16.
- XLV was about 186 on Nov 17, down 0.8% that morning on UnitedHealth, which was down about 5%. That makes your basket's +0.3% relative to XLV partly a function of XLV's own weakness.

## Read for a 1–10 session hold
- **For a bounce:** Fundamentals are intact, with guidance raised at NTRA, GH, TEM, ADPT, NEO and TWST (TWST's FY27 guide is 21% growth). The selloff followed no news and looks like deleveraging, and the basket is stretched to 2.0 standard deviations below its norm.
- **Against a bounce:** There is no turn yet. NTRA fell again today, and the Nov 16 weakness had no identified cause, so selling pressure may not be finished. The Nov 6 NTRA drop included a CEO change and insider selling. Valuations were very high before the drop.
- **Specific risks and events in the window:**
  - The final CMS Clinical Laboratory Fee Schedule (CLFS) rates, which matter most for ADPT.
  - Any further news on the Natera CEO transition.
  - The Personalis closing for TEM.
  - Broader AI and tech risk-off moves.
- **Caution on the data:** Price quotes for the same date differ by several percent across secondary sources (NTRA on Nov 16, TWST on Nov 12). I did not verify against exchange data.

**Bottom line:** Today's move looks like a flight from software, with a pocket of payroll strength underneath. The group is up against IGV mostly because IGV is falling harder. The coverage I found was thin and partly inconsistent, so treat the details below with that in mind.

**What is driving today (Nov 17)**
- Software is being sold broadly ahead of an expected Anthropic IPO, on top of the ongoing "AI eats SaaS" fear. Salesforce was down about 7–10% intraday, Workday about 4.8% at $184.81, and ServiceNow about 5–6% ([Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/26/11/63359152/stock-market-today-salesforce-software-selloff-anthropic-ipo-nvidia-november-17), [Proactive](https://www.proactiveinvestors.com/companies/news/1101949/salesforce-leads-wall-street-software-sell-off-as-investors-brace-for-anthropic-ipo-1101949.html), [TradingKey](https://tradingkey.com/news/market-movers/262309214-market-movers-crm-20261117)).
- Workday's drop has no company-specific catalyst. One report (dated Nov 18, so I'd distrust it) gives a close of $185.25, down 4.54%, and blames AI-disruption and valuation worries ([JKN](https://news.jkn.co.kr/editions/english/post/1102777)). Today's session is still open, so that close can't be real.
- Background: IGV fell about 28% in H1 2026 and had its worst quarter since 2008 in Q1 ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/04/09/anthropic-new-ai-agent-software-stocks-selloff.html), [StockTwits](https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/igv-etf-logs-worst-quarter-since-2008-crisis-salesforce-service-now-workday-lose-over-30/cZ7xpDYRI8d)). ServiceNow fell 19% on its late-October earnings and about 30% in a month ([24/7 Wall St.](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/29/servicenow-tumbles-19-as-slower-contract-growth-overshadows-raised-ai-target-salesforce-slides-6-workday-drops-5/)). Workday dropped about 5% that day too.

**Why the other four are holding up: fundamentals are solid, and they are priced as payroll or "real economy" names rather than pure software**
- **ADP:** The fiscal Q1 report on Oct 28 had revenue up 6% and adjusted EPS up 13% to $2.82. US pays per control rose 2%, ahead of plan. The full-year pays-per-control outlook was raised to about 1%, and revenue growth to about 6%, with higher client-funds interest income ([Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/adp-q1-fiscal-2027-slides-13-eps-growth-raised-outlook-93CH-4979608), [Fool transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/10/28/adp-adp-q1-2027-earnings-call-transcript/)). Cantor raised its target to $336 on Oct 30. The ex-dividend date is Dec 11 ($1.90). The caveat is that revenue retention is still guided down 10–30 bp.
- **Paycom:** Q3 on Nov 4 had revenue of $543.8M, up 10.2%, and non-GAAP EPS of $3.37. Guidance was raised for the second time this year, to $2.213–2.218B and adjusted EBITDA of $1.069–1.079B. Margin was 49.3% and management cited AI adoption. Implied Q4 growth slows to about 8% on a tough comparison ([SEC 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001590955/000119312526447248/payc-ex99_1.htm), [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9173826/paycom-software-inc-payc-q3-2026-earnings-call-highlights-revenue-climbs-10-as-ai-adoption-accelerates-and-guidance-raised-again)). One source has it up about 46% year to date, and I couldn't confirm that.
- **Paylocity:** Fiscal Q1 on Nov 6 had revenue of $451.7M, up 11%, which beat the top of guidance by $7.2M. It raised full-year revenue guidance by $30M to $1.910–1.925B, which implies only about 8% growth. Recurring revenue growth is guided to about 9%, which some read as decelerating ([Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/paylocity-announces-first-quarter-fiscal-210500725.html), [Panabee](https://www.panabee.com/news/paylocity-earnings-q1-2027)). That is near the top of its $92.99–185.93 range and above the $177.82 consensus target ([Investing.com](https://investing.com/news/company-news/paylocity-stock-hits-52week-high-at-18161-usd-93CH-5030426)). Stretched.

agents.report:
**UUUU research summary, as of about 12:10 PM CT on Tuesday 2026-11-17**

**Bottom line:** I found no UUUU-specific news today. The stock is falling for three reasons that stack: its own equity supply, a rare earth sector selloff, and an unresolved risk in the VAC deal. The uranium business itself is working. I did not read the full ATM filing, the 10-Q or the 8-K amendment, and several of these sources are secondary or aggregators.

**What's pushing the price down**
1. **At-the-market (ATM) share sales.**
   - A new $500M ATM program was filed on Oct 13, and the stock fell about 10% that day to an intraday low of 8.36 ([GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9123599/energy-fuels-uuuu-shares-drop-nearly-10-after-500m-atm-equity-program-announcement), [prospectus supplement](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/UUUU/424b5-energy-fuels-inc-prospectus-supplement-debt-securities-9c92cf7f1fa1.html)).
   - Agents are BMO, Canaccord, Cantor, B. Riley and H.C. Wainwright. Use of proceeds explicitly includes the roughly $718M cash portion of the VAC deal.
   - Management said on the Q3 call it would use the program "with discipline" and disclosed no usage ([call summary](https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262289240-)). Shares sold earlier this year went for about $18 net, and the stock is now near $6.
   - So there is a standing overhang, and I couldn't tell how much has been sold.
2. **VAC deal risk.** VAC is Vacuumschmelze, a rare earth magnet maker.
   - Energy Fuels agreed to buy it for about $1.9B: roughly $718M cash plus 65.85M new shares, with Ara Partners ending up at about 19.9%.
   - The deal is expected to close in early 2027, pending regulatory approvals.
   - GM terminated its supply contract with VAC's Sumter, SC plant, and the VAC unit e-VAC Magnetics filed for arbitration ([Rare Earth Exchanges](https://rareearthexchanges.com/news/gm-vac-magnet-contract-terminated/)). An Oct 13 amendment added purchase price adjustment mechanisms tied to the dispute, but no amount has been disclosed ([Panabee](https://www.panabee.com/news/energy-fuels-modifies-1-9-billion-vac-merger-terms-amid-customer-dispute)).
   - The Sumter plant has about 2,000 tpa of capacity.
   - The law firm Block & Leviton announced a review of whether investors were misled about the deal. The only sources I found were German-language and from October, and a firm's review is not a finding of wrongdoing ([source](https://trading-treff.de/aktien/energy-fuels-aktie-block-leviton-untersucht-uebernahmeangaben)).
3. **Sector and macro selling.**
   - Rare earth names have been sliding together. USA Rare Earth is down about 37% in a month, and MP Materials dropped 21% in a month ([24/7 Wall St, Nov 17](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/17/usa-rare-earth-drops-7-as-rare-earth-selloff-extends-ahead-of-trump-xi-meeting-critical-metals-slides-5-mp-materials-falls-3/)).
   - Today's articles cite a William Blair downgrade of USA Rare Earth on Nov 16 and positioning ahead of a Trump-Xi meeting. Traders fear a thaw would erode the non-China price premium that supports U.S. rare earth producers.
   - On Nov 10, UUUU fell 8% to 6.69 along with the group. That article blamed a hot October CPI and Fed rate-hike fears ([source](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/10/usa-rare-earth-sinks-11-as-q3-miss-overshadows-first-magnet-sales-energy-fuels-retreats-8-mp-materials-falls-5/)).
   - Uranium equities are weak too. URNM closed Nov 16 at its lowest since May 2025 and is down about 31% this year while spot is up about 10%. One Substack author blames AI-trade deleveraging and rates above 5% ([source](https://uranium2035.substack.com/p/why-is-urnm-down-november-2026)). This is opinion.
   - The Nov 5 selloff hit UUUU almost three times as hard as URNM.

**Q3 results (Nov 4)** ([press release](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/energy-fuels-announces-q3-2026-results-302929846.html))
- **Revenue and loss:**
  - Revenue was $29.2M, up 65%.
  - The loss was $0.20 per share against a consensus of about -$0.10, on a net loss of about $52M.
  - $35.3M of that loss was non-cash mark-to-market losses on securities.
- **Uranium:**
  - 320k lb sold at $88.90/lb against a cost of about $34/lb, a roughly 63% margin.
  - Pinyon Plain grade was 1.04%, up from 0.71% in Q2 but below management's expectations.
  - Long-term contract deliveries for 2026 are essentially complete.
  - The White Mesa mill was idle in Q3 and should restart around Dec 1.
- **Balance sheet:** Working capital was $932M, but $779M of that is marketable securities and cash is only $76M. There is no convertible debt.
- **Rare earths:**
  - The ASM acquisition closed in August and brought the Korean Metals Plant and the Dubbo project.
  - ASM's near-term contribution is expected to be limited.
  - The heavy rare earth build-out at White Mesa is targeted for early 2028, with about $100M of spending mostly in 2027.
- **Donald project (Australia):** A final investment decision is targeted by the end of 2026, with conditional debt of up to A$180M.

**Other items**
- **Government loan:** A $725M loan commitment from the Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital was announced June 18. It is conditional, and I found no sign it has been finalized ([source](https://pulse2.com/energy-fuels-receives-conditional-725-million-financing-commitment-from-u-s-government/)).
- **Congressional probe:** In August, two House Democrats opened an inquiry into CEO and chairman stock purchases in July. The theory is advance knowledge of the Bears Ears reduction. The company denies wrongdoing ([KJZZ](https://www.kjzz.org/text/politics/2026-08-12/democrats-in-congress-are-investigating-energy-fuels-for-alleged-insider-trading)).
- **Analysts:** The MarketBeat consensus is Moderate Buy with a $19.30 average target. H.C. Wainwright cut its target to $22.50 on Nov 5, B. Riley to $19 on Oct 28, and Zacks went to Strong Sell on Nov 9. Targets are far above the price and look stale ([MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-energy-fuels-nyseamerican-uuuu-reaches-new-52-week-low-whats-next-2026-11-16/)). Market cap is about $1.6B and beta is 1.83.

**Dates and catalysts over the next 1-10 sessions**
- **Trump-Xi meeting:** CNN's Nov 17 live blog reportedly places a bilateral at the APEC summit in Shenzhen. I couldn't open the page (HTTP 451) and found no date. Other sources conflict on the timeline.
- **China's pause:** China extended its pause on new rare earth export controls to Jan 10 ([US News](https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2026-11-09/china-extends-suspension-of-new-rare-earth-controls-until-january)).
- **Possible negatives:** More ATM selling, a VAC arbitration or price adjustment disclosure, a thaw headline, and the Fed and CPI backdrop.
- **Possible positives:** A Donald financial close, a finalized OSC loan, and the White Mesa restart around Dec 1. All three depend on timing the company controls.
- **Uranium spot:** About $90/lb, with the long-term price indicator at a record of about $98-99 ([FNArena](https://fnarena.com/2026/11/17/uranium-week-paladin-taps-market-for-cash/)).

**Data conflicts**
- Price sources disagree. One shows a Nov 16 close of 6.04 and another shows 6.59 as the prior close. Use your own feed.
- The net loss is $52.2M in some outlets and $52.4M in the release.
- I couldn't verify short interest or insider selling.

agents.report:
**HOOD research, 12:10 PM CT Tue 2026-11-17**

**The short version:** HOOD is down about 30% in a month from a stack of negatives, not one shock. The core brokerage business is still healthy. Next earnings are about 12 weeks out, so nothing scheduled forces a re-rating inside your one-to-ten-session window.

**What has hit the stock**
1. **Crypto slump.**
   - Bitcoin was reported below $62k over the weekend, though I couldn't find a dated Nov 17 bitcoin source to confirm it.
   - Q3 crypto revenue fell 55% to $120M.
   - October crypto notional volume was $17.0B, down 21% from September and down 48% year over year.
2. **Soft Q3 print (Oct 27).**
   - Revenue was a record $1.42B, up 12%, and slightly under estimates (about $1.439B in one report).
   - Net income fell 14% to $476M. Diluted EPS was $0.51, down 16%, against about $0.55 expected. Adjusted EPS was $0.60. EPS reporting conflicts across sources.
   - Shares fell roughly 3–5% after hours and kept sliding after.
3. **Kalshi entering stock trading (Nov 16).**
   - The WSJ reported that Kalshi bought broker-dealer FB Securities in July. It plans to launch stock and ETF trading in about two months, though no date is confirmed.
   - HOOD fell about 7.5% Monday while Schwab was roughly flat. That shows the market sees it as an HOOD-specific threat.
   - Robinhood is both Kalshi's biggest distributor (over half its volume; Piper estimated 25–35% of daily volume) and now a rival. Robinhood co-owns the MIAXdx exchange with Susquehanna.
   - A judge also said the CFTC likely overstepped on Kalshi's stock perpetuals. She denied an emergency halt, and the injunction question sits with another judge, with no ruling reported as of Nov 16.
4. **Legal and regulatory.**
   - Louisiana's attorney general sued Kalshi, Polymarket, Robinhood and others on Nov 12 over prediction markets. A state judge signed an ex parte temporary restraining order.
   - Robinhood says its event contracts are CFTC-regulated, and the CFTC has sued Louisiana.
   - Robinhood has also sued Washington state over its gambling laws.
   - A former Robinhood engineer pleaded guilty on Nov 16 to wire fraud for trading on confidential token-listing information. Sentencing is Feb 25, 2027. This looks minor for the stock.
5. **Analyst target cuts.**
   - Goldman cut its target to $115 from $128 on Nov 13 and kept Buy. Cantor cut to $120 from $150 on Nov 2.
   - One source cited an Evercore cut to $100. I found no Evercore cut. Evercore initiated with Outperform and a $130 target on Oct 12. Treat the cut as unverified.
   - Consensus target is around $129–135, far above the price.

**What is still working**
- **Trading volume:** Options revenue rose 31% to $399M and equities revenue rose 41% to $121M. Event contracts brought in $173M, up more than six times. October options contracts were up 8% year over year.
- **Customers and assets:** Funded customers were 28.9M at the end of October. Gold subscribers hit a record 5.2M, up 34%. Platform assets were $396B at the end of Q3 and $383B at the end of October, which is down 3% from September.
- **Net deposits:**
  - They were $15.1B in October, with about $6B from the Dell family's contribution to Trump Accounts.
  - They were $80.5B over twelve months.
- **Margin:** The margin book is a record, around $22–23B. The company said the October drop in cash and deposits "largely reversed in early November".
- **Buybacks:** Management bought back only $25M in Q3, at about $105 a share. Cumulative repurchases are $1.3B. At $68 the stock is far below that, but I found no announced acceleration.
- **Expense guidance:** The 2026 adjusted operating expense and share-based compensation outlook narrowed to $2.675B–$2.75B.
- **Weak spots:** Net interest revenue fell 9%. Securities lending revenue was down 43% year over year.
- **Analyst commentary:** J.P. Morgan called the brokerage a "near-perfect environment for retail traders". Bernstein is bullish on prediction markets, projecting $586M of revenue in 2026 and $1.7B by 2028.

**Technicals (Investing.com, as of Nov 16)**
- All 12 moving-average signals were Sell, and price was below the 20-day, 50-day and 200-day averages.
- RSI was about 29, and ADX was 30.5 with -DI at 39 versus +DI at 16, a strong downtrend.
- Support is the 52-week low of $63.51–63.52, which is also the area of the March low (about $65). Resistance is around $78–80, with the 10-day average near $81.
- A break of the low opens a path lower. One source floated about $40 as a risk scenario, not a target. Reclaiming $80 would be the first sign of stabilization.
- The stock was $72 at Monday's close and about $68 now. It is only about 7% above the 52-week low.

**Calendar**
- **Nov 12:** Louisiana filed suit and won the TRO.
- **Nov 13:** Goldman cut its target.
- **Mid-December:** November operating data is due, probably around Dec 10–15 (an estimate from the October release on Nov 12, not a confirmed date). That is likely the next hard data point, and I'd expect it to show weak crypto volume again.
- **Within about two months:** Kalshi's stock-trading launch.
- **Feb 10, 2027:** Next earnings.

**Read for a 1–10 session trade**
- **Bounce case:** The stock is deeply oversold, the fundamentals for equities, options and deposits are intact, and the Kalshi risk is so far narrative only, with no measured revenue loss. Targets of $78–81 are plausible on a crypto or sentiment rebound.
- **Falling-knife case:** The drop is still accelerating, with two consecutive down days of about 5–7%. Momentum is strong and the stock trades off crypto and headline flow. There is no catalyst from the company, such as a buyback announcement, to stop the slide. A break below $63.5 has little support under it. Further Kalshi, CFTC or state-court headlines could land any day.
- **Where the bounce case could fail:** Today's selling is at $68 on 1.4 times normal volume, with no sign of capitulation yet.

**Source caveats**
- Benzinga and Invezz pages returned 403 errors, so I relied on search summaries for them.
- The Robinhood investor-relations page also returned 403, so Q3 and October figures come from Finviz and Crypto Briefing copies of the releases.
- I did not find the earnings call transcript.

**Expeditors (EXPD), the strongest leg**
- Q3 was reported Nov 3. EPS was $2.65 (+62%) against about $2.22 expected. Revenue was $4.11B (+42%) against about $3.62B expected.
- Air tonnage rose 13% and ocean containers 7%. Operating efficiency was 36.7%, against a 30% target.
- Management ties the strength to hyperscaler and AI data-center air shipments, and expects port congestion to last through year-end.
- The stock closed at $195.34 on Nov 16, near the top of a 52-week range of $129.59 to $207.93. The average price target is about $194, so the stock sits at the target. BofA ($230) and Truist ($200) raised targets.
- **Investor Day is tomorrow, Nov 18, about 7:30 AM to 11:00 AM CT in New York.** It is a scheduled event for the next session. I found no previews of what will be announced.

**C.H. Robinson (CHRW)**
- On Oct 5 CHRW agreed to buy RXO for about $5.8B ($17.25 cash plus 0.0856 CHRW shares, about $30.25 per share).
  - About $3B of new debt funds the cash portion. Buybacks pause after close.
  - It targets $300M of synergies within two years and mid-teens EPS accretion in 2028.
  - Closing is expected in the first half of 2027, pending antitrust review and an RXO vote. I found nothing on a second request.
- The stock fell about 11% the next day, from a deal-reference VWAP near $152 to about $125 to $135.
- Analysts mostly cut targets and kept ratings: BofA to $203, Jefferies to $180, Raymond James to $163, Susquehanna to $166. TD Cowen (Hold, $152) and Bernstein (Market Perform, $151) are skeptical, while StoneX (Buy, $205) called the drop overdone.
- Q3 on Oct 28 was strong. Adjusted EPS was $1.80 against $1.72 expected, adjusted gross profit rose 14.5%, and truckload gross profit per shipment rose 17%.
- The stock was about $134 on Nov 12 after a 3.7% gain on Nov 11, with a 52-week low of $122.21. It is still down about 18% for the year, so it is rebounding off lows.
- One source ties the Nov 11 gain to a dividend increase. I could not confirm that.

**UPS**
- Q3 on Oct 27: adjusted EPS $1.69 against $1.63, and full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised to $7.28. The stock rose about 5% to about $105 and was about $111 more recently.
- UPS is deliberately cutting low-margin Amazon volume. Q4 US daily volume is guided down about 1.3%. US Domestic profit rose 50%, but Supply Chain Solutions profit fell 82%.
- Management cites about $3B of savings from "Efficiency Reimagined." Ex-dividend was Nov 16, a $1.64 payout.
- The shipping industry expects holiday volume up about 4%, with Amazon Shipping taking share.

- FDX fell about 18% when FedEx Freight (FDXF) spun off on June 1, so the 52-week range ($209 to $345) is distorted.

**Bottom line.** The basket's -6.9% is mostly one stock-specific event, not a sector event. Red Cat (RCAT) reported a huge miss and pulled its guidance, and it fell roughly 30-34%. In the one same-day article that gave peer moves, the others were down only about 1% (ONDS -0.9%, AVAV -0.8%, KTOS "quiet"). A header in that article had larger figures (ONDS -5.2%, AVAV -3.6%, KTOS -0.7%) that its own body contradicts. Below the Red Cat shock sits a real sector derating that has run for weeks: a growth and AI-linked selloff, plus company-specific overhangs. I found no same-day macro or defense-news catalyst for the other five names, but I could not read today's market wrap, so "no catalyst" means none found.

**Red Cat (RCAT), the cause of the basket drop**
- Fiscal Q3 revenue was $11.77M against about $40.7M expected. That is up 22% year over year but roughly a 70% miss. Gross profit was only $65K. The loss was $0.26 per share against about $0.18-0.21 expected.
- Management withdrew the full-year 2026 revenue target ($150-180M had been the prior guide) and gave no Q4 guide.
- The stated causes are slow contract awards and funding, and RCAT's FANG FPV drone not being selected as a finalist in Drone Dominance Phase II (Gauntlet II). The CFO tied the shortfall to that. Sources differ on the wording and I did not see the primary filing.
- The stock was about $2.32-2.47, a new 52-week low, and is down roughly 55-71% year to date. Stocktwits called it the worst day since June 2021.
- Cash is about $243M, so there is no near-term solvency issue. Dilution is a concern: weighted shares are 152.8M against 99.6M a year ago.
- The Steyr Motors acquisition is proposed. Ahead are Blue Ops contracts (a potential pipeline of about $2.3B), an Anduril Swarm Forge team slot with demos in January 2027, and a first U.S. government purchase order for the B-26.
- Needham cut its target from $15 to $5 but kept Buy. H.C. Wainwright cut from $20 to $10 and kept Buy. Consensus is still Buy-leaning (consensus target $15.57, now stale). Retail sentiment on Stocktwits moved to "extremely bearish."
- Read: the thesis broke on the near-term revenue path. Further analyst downgrades and target cuts are plausible, and I would expect continued heavy volume.

**Ondas (ONDS)**
- Q3 was a record: revenue $167.5M against $148M expected, backlog $835M, and the 2026 revenue target raised to at least $550M. It also set an initial 2027 target of at least $1.1B.
- The weak spots are GAAP gross margin of 21.8% (adjusted 34.8%, Q4 guided to the mid-30s) and a loss that was flattered by $125M of non-cash warrant gains. About $431M of cash went to acquisitions in Q3, which raises integration and dilution worries.
- Cash and short-term investments are about $820M. Short interest was about 43% of float as of Oct 30.
- The stock has fallen on nearly every recent report despite good news. Examples: -9% on Nov 10 and -5% on Nov 12 (the day after it reported), and -8% to about $4.77 on Nov 16. It is down about 51% year to date.
- Read: this is the highest-beta, most heavily shorted name here. It is a "good news, still sold" tape, but squeezes are possible.

**AeroVironment (AVAV)**
- The company is a profitable prime contractor (Switchblade, Puma, LOCUST). It reaffirmed FY27 revenue guidance of $2.125-2.225B and adjusted EPS of $3.02-3.34 on Sept 9. Q1 revenue was about $480M and funded backlog about $1.5B.
- The stock was about $108.60 and down about 0.8% in the one same-day snapshot.
- The next earnings report is reportedly Dec 8, after the close. The date is confirmed on one site only, and that is outside a 1-10 session window if you hold only that long.
- Read: it is the most defensive of the six and held up best on the fundamentals, though it has also been sliding with the group in recent days.

**Kratos (KTOS)**
- Q3 revenue was $471.8M (up 36%, 23% organic), roughly in line. Adjusted EPS was $0.24 against $0.21 expected. Book-to-bill was 2.2 and backlog $2.65B. Full-year revenue guidance was narrowed to $1.78-1.81B, with Q4 around $495M, above consensus.
- The stock still fell about 7% after the report. Further weakness followed: a downgrade on Nov 10, -5.3% on Nov 12, and -6.6% to about $31.66 on Nov 16 (reported as tied to insider selling). It made 52-week lows near $31.56 and is down roughly 46-55% from the prior year or the start of the year, depending on the source.
- BTIG cut its target from $104 to $65 and KeyBanc also cut its target. Valuation compression is the theme, not a business problem.
- Read: it was quiet today, but it is in a persistent downtrend with analysts still far above the price.

**Unusual Machines (UMAC)**
- Q3 revenue was $13.9M (up 551% year over year, down from $16.7M in Q2). Gross margin was 35.4%. The GAAP loss of $0.50 per share is mostly non-cash, and the adjusted EBITDA loss was about $0.7M. Cash is about $162M, and inventory rose to $65.9M.
- It guided Q4 revenue to about $25M, driven by Drone Dominance and counter-drone orders. The CEO targets positive adjusted EBITDA in 2027. The stock was about $10.84 on Nov 16 (-4%).
- Its Q4 guide leans on the same Drone Dominance funding and timing that just hurt RCAT. That is the closest read-across risk in the group. Gurufocus's headline cited "supply constraints."

**AEVEX (AVEX)**
- It IPO'd on NYSE in April at $20, roughly doubled in two sessions, and then fell back. On Nov 12 it rose more than 13% after Q3: revenue +56.5% to $189.7M, EBITDA +73% to $30.8M. It raised 2026 revenue guidance to $820-840M from $700-720M and adjusted EBITDA to $128-132M from $105-111.5M.

- Overhangs: a securities class action over the alleged waiver of the IPO lock-up, and a June secondary at $27 where the sponsor sold 8M shares. Lock-up expiry was set for Oct 13, so that supply risk is now live.
- It is the only name of the six with a clear beat-and-raise, which fits it being the best performer today.

- The Nov 16 selloff was blamed on reports of a possible NVIDIA leadership change hitting AI-linked growth stocks, with the Nasdaq 100 down about 1.4% and small, high-beta drone names hit hardest. Earlier mentions in mid-November cited rate-hike fears and profit-taking.

Drone Dominance Gauntlet II picked nine vendors for about 60,000 one-way attack drones. The winners were mostly private or non-basket names: Neros (14,000 drones), Perennial Autonomy, Skycutter, Vector and Swarm Defense. None of the six public names is a named winner. Gauntlet III and a Bomber Challenge are still pending. That is a near-term catalyst for UMAC and RCAT either way.
- I found no evidence of a Ukraine ceasefire or budget-shutdown driver this month. Older episodes were mostly European defense names.

**Setup for a 1-10 session decision**
- A correlated, momentum-negative group with no name above its 50-day average. Realized volatility is 2.3 times the prior 50 sessions.
- Today's basket drop is idiosyncratic to RCAT, so a mean-reversion bet on the basket is mostly a bet on the other five. Those five were down only about 1% or less, or up (AVEX), in the same-day sources I could read, so they have not yet "dropped" in the same way.

- Event risks to watch: further RCAT analyst actions and a possible equity raise, UMAC read-across, and ONDS acquisition and financing news. AVAV earnings on Dec 8 fall outside the window. I found no confirmed ONDS, KTOS or AVEX earnings dates inside the next ten sessions.

**SNDK research brief, 12:10 PM CT, Tue 2026-11-17**

Several sources are secondary aggregators, and a few key claims could not be confirmed. Those are flagged below.

**The story in short**
- The business is strong. The stock is being sold on fears about when the NAND cycle peaks, plus a broad AI-hardware selloff, not on a company-specific problem.
- Fiscal Q1 2027 (quarter ended Oct 2, reported Oct 29) beat Sandisk's own guidance:
  - Revenue was $11.03B, up 23% from the prior quarter and up about 378% from a year earlier.
  - Non-GAAP gross margin was 85.1%, and non-GAAP EPS was $49.51 against guidance of $44–46.
  - Datacenter revenue was $4.8B, up 61% from the prior quarter. Consumer revenue fell 39% from a year earlier, to $397M.
  - The company bought back about $5B of stock.
- Q2 guidance:
  - Revenue of $12.2–12.6B and EPS of $55–57 before the split.
  - Management said "pricing to continue to increase modestly" and that its customer pipeline exceeds supply through the end of the decade.
  - One Q2 note says fiscal Q3 is usually the weakest quarter, so Q2 assumptions are conservative.
- Valuation is about 4.5 times trailing sales, per Trefis.
- The stock is roughly 66% below its June peak. Trefis puts the June 25 close at $2,335 and the 52-week closing low at $194 (Dec 2025). Since the Nov 11 close of $977.69 it has fallen about 20%.
- It fell 50.5% over the three months to Nov 13. It is still up about 240% year to date, per Trefis.

**Recent price path**
- Nov 5: SNDK fell about 22% and Micron about 17%, in an AI-chip and memory selloff. I found no clear primary explanation for that day.
- Nov 12: down 4.1%.
- Nov 13: down 5.6% with no company news. Trefis blames a selloff in AI hardware after a report that Nvidia's CEO resigned. Only one site (FourWeekMBA) reports the resignation, so it is unverified.
- Nov 16: down 8.58% to $809.11, a third straight loss. The move started before any news.

  - 24/7 Wall St. reported a GF Securities note that cut its NAND price forecast. It sees flat prices in Q1 2027, then declines over three quarters, and warns of an oversupply glut in 2027.
  - It said Sandisk, as a pure NAND maker, faces the most earnings volatility.

**Catalysts and dates inside your 1–10 session window**
