**IGV research, Tuesday 2026-11-17, about 12:10 PM CT**

**Bottom line:** Today's drop looks like flow and positioning pressure, not a company-specific or fundamental shock. Three overlapping events drive it: the Anthropic IPO, Nvidia earnings tonight, and the long-running fear that AI agents will cut software seat counts. The most important dates fall inside your 1-10 session window. The IPO prices the evening of Nov 18 and trades Nov 19. Because the news cuts both ways, I'd call this a high-variance setup and not a clean directional edge.

**What is happening today**
- **Software sold off hard, on no news.**
  - Salesforce fell about 9.7% to $194.09, the worst stock in the S&P 500, with no company news. Yahoo attributes it to seat-priced software sliding ahead of Anthropic's IPO, and to funds selling software to raise cash for the roughly $64B offering.
  - HubSpot fell 7%, ServiceNow 7% (no news) and Workday 5%. Benzinga has Intuit down about 6.7% and ServiceNow about 6.5%.
  - Benzinga's midday note says IGV was down about 3.4%, its fifth drop of 3% or more since Oct 16. A later report had it down 4.4%. Your 3.7% at 95.36 sits in that range.
  - RBC's Rishi Jaluria is quoted as saying "the AI companies are going to try to destroy Salesforce entirely." TipRanks also mentions a Salesforce data breach, but the Yahoo piece doesn't. Treat the breach as unconfirmed.
- **Broad market is weak.** AP says AI stocks are still swinging, with Nvidia down 2.9%. Nvidia closed Monday at $156.14 after falling 4.1%, and it has fallen six straight weeks, the longest streak since 2012. I could not open the AP/Washington Times and Benzinga pages (HTTP 403), so those details come from search summaries.

**Catalysts in your window**
- **Nvidia earnings tonight (Nov 17)**, after the close, call at 5 PM ET. Consensus is about $109B revenue and $2.47 EPS.
  - This is the first report since Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO.
  - Guidance, Vera Rubin demand and the CEO search are the watch items.
  - The reaction will likely move all of tech, including IGV.
- **Anthropic IPO:** pricing the evening of Nov 18, first trade Nov 19 on Nasdaq as ANT, contingent on the SEC declaring the S-1 effective.
  - The range is $70-78 for 825M shares, raising about $58-64B.
  - Fully diluted valuation is about $1.26-1.41T. Bankers reportedly expect pricing above the range.
  - Anthropic launched its own Sheets, Data, Meetings and Whiteboards tools ahead of the IPO. IGV fell 1.1% and ServiceNow 3.1% on that news last week.
- **Workday earnings** Nov 24 after the close. **Salesforce earnings** Dec 2.

**The bull and bear cases**
- **Bear case (Trefis, Nov 12, partly promotional):**
  - Per-seat pricing is threatened because AI agents do the work.
  - ANT's valuation is 2.4-2.7x the combined $516B of Salesforce, ServiceNow, Adobe, Intuit and Workday.
  - Investors can now buy the disruptor directly, so spending could shift from incumbents to Anthropic.
- **Bull and mitigating case:**

  - Salesforce says its Agentforce seats grew, and ServiceNow says 50% of its net new business is not priced per seat.

- Software has had repeated AI-disruption sell-offs: a Citrini note, an Anthropic agent launch in January, and ServiceNow falling 27% in one day on Oct 29.
- Per ZeroHedge, IGV fell roughly 37% from its September peak, then reclaimed its 200-day average in late May.

# NTNX research brief, 12:10 PM CT, Tue 2026-11-17

## Bottom line
I found no company-specific bad news behind the slide. The stock looks like it is falling with a broad risk-off market, on top of a lack of buyers and valuation compression after a strong run. The search tool returned no fresh Nutanix news from the last few days, so I can't fully rule out an unseen catalyst. The real event is the earnings report in six sessions. Nutanix has a history of large earnings moves, and it fell 17% on the last November report. Over a 1 to 10 session hold, the trade is mostly a bet on the earnings print plus the market tape.

## What drove the decline (about $68 to $56 over 20 sessions)
- **Market tape:** On Nov 16 the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.49% and the S&P 500 fell 1.92%. The Nasdaq is more than 10% off its October high. Reported drivers:
  - Nvidia leadership uncertainty.
  - New chip-export licensing rules.
  - Treasury yields above 5%.
  - A VIX jump of about 19%.
  - Nvidia was reported to report later today (Nov 17), which is a swing factor for tech sentiment. I could not confirm the exact time.
- **Software and AI backdrop:** Software has been weak all year on AI-disruption fears. One report put the software index down about 20 to 25% for 2026. I found no Nov 2026 specifics.
- **NTNX's own slide began in October:**
  - Oct 14: -4.2% to about $69.85.
  - Oct 16: -4.3% to $66.96.
  - Oct 30: -5.0% to $67.21.
  - Nov 2: -4.1% to $64.43.
  - Nov 4: $63.70.
  - Nov 13: about $60.38.
  - Nov 16: $58.94 close, -2.4%.
  - Today: $56.25 (your screen figure).
  - Gurufocus and other valuation pieces gave no catalyst for these drops. I found no downgrade, guidance change or competitor shock in November.
- **Insider selling in October:**
  - CFO Rukmini Sivaraman sold 232,712 shares on Oct 12 at about $74.55 (about $17.4M). That cut her direct holding by 71.5%.
  - A director sold 3,500 shares on Oct 9 at $73.67.
  - Insiders sold about 674k shares (about $49.7M) over 90 days, with no buying.
  - That may be a sentiment overhang. Selling right near the highs is not a good look.

## The fundamental story
- **Q4 FY26 (reported Aug 26, quarter ended July 31):**
  - Revenue was $757.1M, up 15.9%, against a $738M consensus.
  - Adjusted EPS was $0.60 against $0.49 expected.
  - ARR was $2.55B, up 16%. Net dollar retention was 106%.
  - The company added 650 customers in the quarter, for 32,360 in total.
  - FY26 free cash flow was $841M, a 29% margin.
  - The stock rose about 6% after hours on the report.
- **Guidance:**
  - Q1 FY27 revenue is $755 to $765M, about 13.3% growth at the midpoint, a slowdown from 16%. The non-GAAP operating margin guide is 26 to 28%.
  - FY27 revenue is $3.18 to $3.23B, about 12.5% growth, roughly in line with the $3.20B consensus.
  - FY27 free cash flow is $850 to $950M.
  - Gross margin slipped to 86.0% from 87.2%.
- **Headwinds:**
  - Server prices are up and supply is constrained. The CEO sees "no near-term letup" through FY27.
  - Management expects more future-start-date deals, which push revenue recognition out.
  - Growth from traditional HCI and VMware-migration customers is slowing. The company is pivoting to external storage (Dell, NetApp and Everpure support), AI and Kubernetes.
  - About 5% of staff (roughly 400 jobs) were cut. Restructuring charges are $33 to $43M, with about $30 to $35M of cash paid in Q1.
  - Trefis notes the pool of renewing contracts grows more slowly as the base gets larger.
- **Valuation:**
  - The headline 11x P/E is misleading. A one-time $1.2B tax benefit made up about 80% of FY26 GAAP profit.
  - Excluding it, GAAP EPS is $1.04. Non-GAAP EPS is $2.04, and the FY27 consensus is $2.33, so the stock trades at about 25x forward.
  - The free cash flow yield is about 5%. Net cash is about $843M. Market cap is about $16.3B.
  - Beta is 0.72, but the stock has been trading with the high-beta tape.

## Analysts
- MarketBeat on Nov 15 showed a "Moderate Buy" consensus (10 Buy, 9 Hold) with an average target of $74.87.
- Late-August moves were mostly raises:
  - Wells Fargo went to $65 (equal weight).
  - KeyBanc went to $75 (overweight).
  - UBS set $85.
  - Oppenheimer went to $85 (outperform).
- Needham initiated at Buy with a $90 target on Sep 28.
- I found no November 2026 rating changes.
- A Guggenheim Buy with a $100 target appears in sources, but they give no year. I'm treating it as unverified.

## Earnings setup (Nov 24)
- **Date:** Yahoo says Nutanix reports Nov 24. A tick-based site says Nov 23. I found no company date announcement. Last year's report was after the close on Nov 25, 2025, so Nov 24 after the close is plausible.
- **Typical move:** Sources put the average day-after move at about 8.6 to 13.8%. The options market has implied about 13 to 15% in recent quarters. The August 2026 report was implied at ±14.9% and realized +6.8%.
- **Skew:** The worst recent reaction was -17.1% on 2025-11-25, after a Q1 revenue and Q2 outlook miss. The Feb 2026 reaction was +4%.
- **What to watch:**
  - Q1 revenue against the guide of $755 to $765M.
  - ARR growth. A sharp drop below 16% would hurt the multiple.
  - The mix of future-start-date deals.
  - Gross margin.
  - Any change to FY27 guidance.
  - Signs that external storage is ramping.
- **Why it could go either way:**
  - The shares are down about 22% from the high going in, so some bad news may already be priced.
  - The Q1 guide was set conservatively after a beat, and the last print was received well.
  - Against that, the multiple is still about 25x forward and the macro tape is weak.

## Timing and what I could not confirm
- **Next 1 to 3 sessions:** Nvidia's report is a market-wide swing factor. A relief rally in tech would likely lift a stock down 17.5% in twenty sessions. Continued selling could take it toward the 200-day (53.52).
- **Technical levels:**

agents.report:
**AAOI research, 12:10 PM CT, Tue 2026-11-17**

**Bottom line:** AAOI is a high-beta AI-optics stock in a sector-wide drawdown, with a company-specific wobble from the November 5 earnings report. The business is growing fast, but the fundamental picture got slightly worse in the last two weeks. No scheduled catalyst I could find lands inside the next 1-10 sessions except a possible second long-term supply agreement (LTA), which management says is weeks away. The screen's reading of a falling stock below its 20-day low matches the news flow. I found no new company-specific bad news today.

**What happened**
- **Peak and decline:** The stock peaked around $233 and was about $160 in August. Insiders sold heavily at $100-110 in September and October. It then fell about 59% in the month to Nov 5.
- **Oct 15, Oct 30:** Down 6% and 15%. The Oct 30 drop was on hyperscaler spending fears.
- **Nov 3-4:** Up 5% on Nov 3. On Nov 4, AI stocks sold off after reports that Democrats won both houses of Congress. Investors feared tighter data-center rules.
- **Nov 5, earnings:** Sources conflict. Several describe a drop of about 16-18% to near $50. A Yahoo/Zacks-type piece says shares rose 7% after earnings. Per Benzinga, the stock fell despite the beat. Treat the move as a large drop, with the exact figure unverified.
- **Nov 9-13:**
  - Optics stocks rebounded Nov 9 (AAOI +4%), and AAOI was up 12% on Nov 11.
  - On Nov 12 it fell 4% to about $54. A proposed FCC ban on new Chinese-made transceivers ran into pushback from Microsoft and others.
  - On Nov 13 it fell 5.6% to about $49.89.
- **Nov 16, Monday:** Down about 9% to roughly $45 (Benzinga), on AI funding worries, Nvidia uncertainty and rate-hike fears.
- **Today:** Google Finance showed about $44.16, down 2.2%, with a day range of $42.65 to $48.22. That is a wide intraday range, so it is a volatile tape.

**Q3 report (Nov 5)**

| Item | Result |
|---|---|
| Revenue | $269.9M, up 127% year over year, sixth straight record quarter |
| Non-GAAP EPS | $0.17, versus about $0.14 expected |
| GAAP net income | $6.3M, first GAAP profit in a while |
| Non-GAAP gross margin | 28.7%, below the 29-30.5% guide; blamed on more 400G mix after a customer moved to 1.6T faster than expected |
| Q4 revenue guide | $385-420M |
| Q4 gross margin guide | 29.5-31%, versus earlier talk of 32-33% |

- **Weak points in the report:**
  - The Q4 revenue guide was reported as below estimates (Benzinga, Seeking Alpha: "soft datacenter revenue, weak Q4 outlook").
  - Expected 1.6T revenue in Q4 is $50-70M, down from the $70-80M previously indicated, due to chip (DSP) constraints.
  - End-2026 capacity of 800G and 1.6T units per month was cut from 650k to over 500k. The Texas Phase 2 build slipped on electrical power.
  - The $471M monthly revenue target moved from mid-2027 to end-2027.
- **Customer concentration:** The top 10 customers were 99% of revenue. One cable-TV customer was 41%, and two datacenter customers were 28% and 23%. Microsoft was 28.8% of 2025 revenue.
- **Balance sheet and funding:**
  - Q3 capex was $501M. Cash rose to $621.5M, mostly from at-the-market share sales.
  - Payables are $494M and inventory $378M.
  - A new $200M bank loan was signed, with a possible expansion to $400-500M.
  - Q4 diluted shares are guided to about 96M, up from 87.8M. Share count was about 49M at the end of 2024.
  - Amazon holds a warrant on up to about 7.9M shares at about $23.70.
- **Management contradictions:** The CFO said capex would keep rising in 2027, and the CEO said it would not. Management said no customers are second-guessing AI spending.

**The bull story**
- **New supply agreement:** A multi-year LTA was signed in October with an existing Tier 1 hyperscaler, for 1.6T only. It runs June 2026 to May 2029 and covers at least 10% of that customer's 1.6T needs. AOI expects $1-1.5B in value, but the customer committed no capital and there is no prepayment. Pricing steps down over the term.
- **Second LTA:** The CEO said a second LTA is in final stage, expected "within a few weeks," at five times the first or more. It is unsigned, so it could be a pop if announced or a disappointment if delayed.
- **Demand and capacity:** Management says demand exceeds capacity through mid-2027. Capacity should exceed 1M units per month by end-2027.
- **Possible tariff and ban benefit:** AAOI could benefit if the US restricts Chinese transceivers. However, AAOI also manufactures in Ningbo, China and Taipei. The FCC has set no vote date, and the draft reportedly targets 3.2T-class products. Microsoft's pushback undercuts the idea.
- **Consensus:** Consensus is "Moderate Buy" with an average target of about $111.
  - Needham cut its target to $100 (Buy).
  - Rosenblatt cut to $115 (Buy).
  - Raymond James trimmed to $165.
  - Northland upgraded to outperform with a $120 target on Nov 2.
  - B. Riley cut to $45 (Neutral). That is roughly where the stock trades now.

**The bear story**
- **Dilution and cash burn:** Roughly $1.6B of equity was raised in 2026, with free cash flow about -$600M trailing. Capex is far ahead of cash generation. The stock has been funded by selling shares at much higher prices, so a lower price makes further raises more dilutive.
- **Margins:** Gross margin is about 29%. The long-term 40% target is only verbal. LTA price reductions pressure it further.
- **Insider selling:** The CEO sold about $10M in May. Directors sold in March, May, September and the CFO in October. Insiders sold about $6M in the last three months.
- **Concentration and sector crowding:** The stock moves with the sector. Lumentum is down about 40% in a month. Beta is about 4, with a market cap of about $4.5B and average volume of about 10.7M shares.
- **Macro:** Rate-hike fears, AI-funding worries and post-election data-center regulation risk are all weighing on the group.

**Sector tape this week:** Optics names were weak in Monday and Tuesday premarket, led by Lumentum and Coherent. The Marvell-Lumentum all-stock deal has some questioning whether it holds. The Commerce Department is closing loopholes on Chinese AI compute leasing. Nvidia has been weak. Nvidia's earnings are reportedly Nov 25 after the close (a single source, unconfirmed), which is probably outside a 10-session window only if the window ends before it. It is likely inside the window if the hold runs long enough. Check this before relying on it.

**For the 1-10 session decision**
- **Case for a bounce:** The stock is oversold (RSI 32), has fallen about 42% in 20 sessions, and sits at B. Riley's $45 target. Optics names bounced sharply at times (+12% Nov 11, and Coherent +13% Nov 9). The second LTA is a possible near-term upside event.
- **Case against:** Trend is down, below falling 50- and 200-day averages. Each rebound has failed. Sector selling is continuing, and dilution means supply overhang. A late Nvidia-linked or macro scare could take it lower.
- **Risk:** Daily swings of 5-10% are normal. Position sizing and stops should assume that.

**Gaps and caveats**
- I could not open Benzinga (blocked).
- I could not confirm today's headline cause beyond sector weakness.
- I could not verify short interest, the Nov 25 Nvidia date, the exact earnings-day move, or the ATM sizes (sources gave $180M, $250M, $500M and $600M, likely successive programs).
- The "$71M 800G order" item dated November is actually from April 2026.

- **SPG** (reported Nov 5):
  - Real Estate FFO was $3.37, up 4.7%, and full-year FFO guidance rose $0.10 to $13.30-$13.40.
  - Mall and outlet occupancy was 96.5%, the highest since 2016, and comparable sales grew 4.9%.

  - 2027 guidance will wait until February.
  - Analysts are mostly Neutral. Citi raised its target to $237 from $230 today. UBS went to $235 from $205 on Nov 11. Evercore is at $227. Piper Sandler is Overweight at $254. The stock closed near $233 on Nov 13, which is near or above most targets.
- **O** (reported about Nov 2-3):
  - AFFO was $1.12, up 3.7%, and full-year AFFO guidance moved to $4.45-$4.46 from $4.44-$4.45, a small raise.
  - Net income guidance was cut. Occupancy is expected above 98.5%.

  - FFO was $1.87, up 5.6%. Full-year FFO guidance rose to $7.54-$7.58 from $7.48-$7.56, which is over 7% growth at the midpoint. The Q4 FFO range is $1.92-$1.96.

  - It bought The Summit in Birmingham, AL, for $508M after quarter-end. Over $600M of asset sales are in process, are not in guidance, and should close in 2027.

- The 10-year Treasury yield is above 5% (one report says about 5.12%), and the 30-year is near 5.5%.

- No dated November sector recap, no XLRE price data, and no news specific to today for any of the five.

**Bottom line:** MNDY's story is a company-specific growth reset from the Nov 9 earnings report. Today's 6.4% drop looks like a sector move on top of that, and I found nothing MNDY-specific today. The search tool is a summarizer, so the figures below come from secondary pages unless I say otherwise.

**What happened at Q3 (reported Nov 9)**
- Q3 beat on every headline number.
  - Revenue was $377.5M, up 19% against guidance of $368–370M and a $369M consensus.
  - Non-GAAP operating income was $89.4M, a record 24% margin.
  - Non-GAAP EPS was $2.14 against about $1.37 expected.
- The stock still fell about 7–10% on the day, from roughly $88 to $80–82. The Q4 guide was the problem.
  - Q4 revenue guide is $380–382M, about 14% growth, against a $385.7M consensus.
  - Q4 non-GAAP operating income guide is $68–70M, about an 18% margin.
  - Full-year revenue was nudged up to $1.473–1.475B, and full-year margin to about 18% from 16%.
- Net dollar retention (NDR) is 108%, down from 109% in Q2 and 110% in Q1. The CFO guides it to 107% by year-end.
- Cash flow was weak in the quarter.
  - Operating cash flow was $20.4M against $95M a year ago.
  - Adjusted free cash flow was $63M, which excludes $47M of restructuring payments.
- Cash and securities are about $1.1B, down from $1.5B in cash at the end of 2025.

**Management's explanation (earnings call)**
- **Restructuring:** The company cut about 20% of staff in July. Headcount is 2,479, down 690 in the quarter. Management admitted it isn't sure the disruption is behind it.
- **Small-business weakness:** Small-business customer additions fell and logo churn rose. Management says this is partly by design as it moves upmarket, and expects it to continue.
- **Longer enterprise sales cycles:** Customers are buying more deliberately as they work out where AI fits.
- **Customer discovery:** Management said discovery is shifting from search to AI channels, so performance marketing works less well. A test moving about 25% of marketing budget to agentic acquisition "didn't convert as much as we wished."
- **Stabilization timeline:** The CFO said stability is "probably a few quarters" away, likely "throughout 2027." The CEO said the transformation continues into 2027. FY2027 guidance comes with the Q4 report on Feb 8.
- **Savings:** Most of the roughly $100M in restructuring savings goes back into AI, compensation and sales capacity, so margins won't expand much.

**The positives**
- Large accounts keep growing.
  - Customers above $100K ARR: 2,127, up 33%.
  - Customers above $500K ARR: 123, up 58%.
  - NDR for accounts above $50K ARR: 114%.
- AI ARR is $36M.
  - Over 30% of $50K+ accounts pay for AI credits.
  - Management says AI ARR is "not incremental yet," since it is part of total ARR.
- Remaining performance obligations (contracted future revenue) are $946M, up 27%.
- The buyback was spent before Q3 (a later search suggests the full $870M program was used by the end of Q2). Q3 had no repurchases and I found no new authorization. That means there is no company bid under the stock.

**Analysts**
- **Downgrades to Hold:** Needham cited new up-market sales headwinds, go-to-market disruption and higher small-customer churn. It said best-case FY27 growth is only in line with Street estimates, and the cost base may need further trimming. Canaccord also cut to Hold, with a target of $90 from $115. Capital One cut to Equal Weight with a $95 target.
- **Other target cuts:** UBS cut to $90, Barclays to $91, Loop to $90, TD Cowen to $95, Jefferies to $90, Wells Fargo to $100, BTIG to $100, Morgan Stanley to $109 and Oppenheimer to $100. Guggenheim held $130 (set Nov 3, before earnings).
- **Consensus:** Hold, with an average target around $103–105. At $74.93 the stock is below almost every target, but the targets were set before today's sector drop.
- **Valuation:** Needham's note put the stock at about 1.5x FY27 revenue.

**Insiders:** Insider selling looks small, and one report said all of the sales were under pre-arranged 10b5-1 plans, which I did not confirm.
- A director sold 2,000 shares on Oct 20 at about $100.
- A Form 144 shows a director proposing to sell 15,000 shares (about $1.16M) around Nov 12.

**Today (Nov 17), from sector coverage rather than MNDY news**
- Seat-based application software is selling off hard on fears that AI agents undermine per-user pricing, and on the Anthropic IPO.
  - Salesforce is down about 9–10%.
  - HubSpot is down about 7%.
  - Workday is down about 5%.
  - The group is down 5–7%.
- The Anthropic IPO is reported to price Wed Nov 18 and trade Thu Nov 19 as ANT, with a $70–78 range and a valuation up to about $1.4T. One view is that funds are selling software to make room for the IPO.
- I could not find MNDY named in any of today's coverage. Its 6.4% drop fits the sector move, which is my inference. The software theme has been running all year: software is down 20% or more in 2026.

**Read for a 1–10 session trade**
- **Why it could bounce:** The stock is oversold (RSI 34), 3 ATR below its 20-day average and well under analyst targets. Profitability is strong, there is $1.1B in cash, and today's selling looks like sector flow.
- **What could keep it down:**
  - The fundamental story is a multi-quarter deceleration. Management says stabilization runs through 2027.
  - There is no buyback support.
  - The sector is under pressure, with the Anthropic IPO on Wed–Thu as a possible further catalyst.
  - The stock is below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages.
- **Catalysts:** There is no MNDY earnings date in the window, since the next one is Feb 8. The window's catalysts are the Anthropic pricing and debut, plus sector rebounds or further drops.
- **My view:** This is a sector-beta trade on a broken-trend stock, not a company-specific mispricing. Don't expect good news from MNDY itself in the window. No turn has shown yet, so any long is a bet that software flows reverse after the IPO. Waiting for stabilization after Nov 19 looks safer than catching it today.

**IJR/IWM, Tuesday 2026-11-17, about 12:10 PM CT**

**Bottom line:** The ratio's rise looks like a risk-off, quality-over-junk move. It is driven mostly by IWM falling, not by IJR rallying. The usual rule is that this ratio follows speculative appetite. The more the market is selling AI and speculative names, the more IJR holds up against IWM. The ratio is now stretched, and the next session or two probably depend on tonight's Nvidia report. I don't see a durable, independent reason for it to keep climbing. Several sources conflict or look unreliable, noted below.

**Structural story (well supported)**
- IJR tracks the S&P SmallCap 600. It requires positive earnings in the latest quarter and over the trailing four quarters. IWM tracks the Russell 2000, which has no profitability rule. ([Yahoo/Motley Fool, Mar 2026](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/iwm-vs-ijr-two-small-155000279.html); [Schwab](https://www.schwab.com/learn/story/sp-600-often-overlooked-small-cap-index))
- About 40% of Russell 2000 companies are unprofitable. That compares with roughly 20-22% of the S&P 600, per Bloomberg figures in the earlier results. ([Morningstar](https://www.morningstar.com/news/marketwatch/20260630245/small-cap-stocks-just-had-their-best-start-to-a-year-since-1991-the-rest-of-2026-could-look-very-different))
- The 2026 rally was led by unprofitable, mostly AI and semiconductor-linked, Russell names. HSBC data in the 24/7 Wall St. piece show them up 45% year to date against 18% for profitable peers. That is why IWM led in sharp risk-on stretches. ([24/7 Wall St.](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/07/16/the-russell-2000-is-having-its-best-year-in-23-years-heres-why-small-caps-are-winning-again/))
- The 24/7 Wall St. ("Forget IWM") piece, sponsored content, compares the S&P 600 fund SPSM with IWM. Through Aug 6, 2026 SPSM was up 23.6% and IWM 21.2%. The piece notes IWM can lead in sharp risk-on rallies. ([article](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/08/08/forget-iwm-the-small-cap-fund-that-screens-out-money-losers-charges-84-less-and-its-winning-by-2-5-points/))
- IJR costs 0.06% against 0.19% for IWM. IWM trades about 23.6M shares a day against about 3.5M for IJR, so IWM is the more liquid one for fast trading. ([ETFdb](https://etfdb.com/tool/etf-comparison/IJR-IWM/))
- IJR sector weights as of Nov 11, 2026: Financials 18.5%, Industrials 18.0%, Consumer Discretionary 13.9%, Technology 12.4%, Health Care 10.7%. I found no 2026 Russell 2000 weights to compare. ([iShares](https://www.ishares.com/us/products/239774/ishares-core-s-p-small-cap-etf-ijr))

**What is driving the tape now**
- The Russell 2000 fell 1.7% on Monday Nov 16, closing at 2,742.94. The cause was a broadening AI and chip sell-off: Broadcom -3.9%, AMD -5.6%, CoreWeave -6.1%. It is still up about 10.5% for the year. ([ad-hoc-news](https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/marktberichte/russell-2000-falls-1-70-prozent-as-nvidia-led-sell-off-weighs-on-small-caps/70526704))
- Nvidia reports after today's close, and AP calls it the next major test for AI. Retail sales and industrial production came out this morning. Fed speakers Waller and Hammack were scheduled today. I couldn't confirm the exact Nvidia date. One source said Nov 19.
- Several reports say Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang resigned or fell suddenly. I only saw this through secondary outlets (ad-hoc-news, BSS, NST). The NST page returned a 403, so treat it as plausible but not confirmed by a primary source.
- Rates are a headwind. Reports cite the 10-year yield around 5.1% and talk of further Fed hikes, with oil and inflation worries tied to the Iran war. The Fed was reported to be holding at 3.75-4.00% with two officials pushing for a hike. I found no CME FedWatch odds, and the sources don't fully agree on direction.
- IWM was $271.75 (-1.67%) in one technical write-up, below its 20-day average ($278.02) and 50-day average ($277.80). Support is $269.34, then $266.93. Resistance is $273.26, then $275.67. That write-up is a crypto-site, low-quality source, and it was published earlier in the day. It said the sell-off came on lighter volume (0.47x the 5-day average). It named no specific catalyst. ([Blockchain.News](https://blockchain.news/news/20261117-price-prediction-iwm-small-caps-slip-into-a-technically))
- A less reliable report had the Russell 2000 up about 0.5% in the morning. That doesn't match your screen showing IWM down about 1.0% at 12:05 PM CT. Use your own quotes.

**Risks to the idea of the ratio staying up**
- Bounce risk for IWM. If Nvidia's results calm the AI sell-off, the speculative Russell names could rebound hard. That would pull the ratio back down quickly. The ratio is 2.0 standard deviations above its 50-day norm and at a 20-day high, so mean reversion is also a risk.

- Volatility is up (the last ten sessions were 1.4x the prior fifty). That fits an event-driven week rather than a quiet trend.

([EY](https://taxnews.ey.com/news/2026-1695-us-section-232-proclamation-establishes-minimum-import-prices-and-a-15-percent-tariff-on-polysilicon-and-derivative-products), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/07/polysilicon-solar-tariffs-donald-trump-us-china-trade-war-energy-semiconductors.html))

**FSLR (First Solar)**

  - Sources conflict on the premium and deal size. One calls it a roughly 7% discount, and values range from $1.32B to $1.52B.

Storage is the growth engine: shipments beat guidance and the backlog is $3.5B. ([SolarQuarter](https://solarquarter.com/2026/08/27/canadian-solar-reports-1-2-billion-q2-2026-revenue-as-record-energy-storage-shipments-offset-solar-module-decline/))

agents.report:
MSFT's drop today looks like a sector move, with no company-specific shock behind it. I found no new fundamental news. Several sources disagree on dates and numbers, which I note below. I could not open MarketBeat or GuruFocus (both returned 403), so those items come only from search summaries.

**Why it is down today**
- Software led the market lower. Benzinga says the software ETF IGV fell 3.4%, its fifth drop of 3% or more since Oct 16. Salesforce was heading for its worst day since May 2024. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 were each down about 0.9%.
- TradingKey says MSFT was the top software stock by turnover. It fell 3.35% against 2.16% for the sector, while GOOGL fell 0.93% and META 1.06%.
- Rates are a headwind. One source puts the 10-year yield near 5.1%. Nvidia reports after the close today, and chip stocks were weak ahead of it.
- Anthropic's IPO is the main theme for software. It prices around Nov 18 at a $70–78 range, with a valuation reported anywhere from $1.0 to $1.5 trillion or more. Microsoft is both a cornerstone buyer and a competitor.
- On Nov 10, Anthropic launched Claude Sheets, Whiteboards and Data, which target Excel and Office. MSFT fell about 2.2–3% that day.
- Commentary also cites doubts about Copilot monetization, regulatory scrutiny, and capex against free cash flow. These are generic worries, not new facts.
- TradingKey calls the move "tactical multiple contraction and systematic de-risking," not a business problem.

**Outage**
- A Microsoft 365 outage ran Nov 12–14, hitting Outlook, Exchange Online, Teams and Copilot. Microsoft says a Windows update deployed to its gateway servers in July introduced a defect. At the worst point, more than 80% of the affected servers were unresponsive.
- Microsoft says it was not a cyberattack. Its final post-incident report is due by Nov 20.
- One article this morning linked the drop to "cybersecurity" worries and a reported NSA network disruption, but the same piece says there was no evidence of an attack. I'd treat that link as weak.

**Fundamentals**
- Fiscal Q1 2027 was reported Oct 28. Adjusted EPS was $4.92 against $4.73 expected. Revenue was about $92B (one source says $92.3B, up 19%).
- Azure grew 48% in constant currency, against guidance of 44–45%. Guidance for the December quarter is 49–50%.
- Commercial remaining performance obligation (contracted backlog) is $677B, up 73%.
- Capex was $45.2B, below the $50.7B expected, because of delayed GPU deliveries. The December quarter is guided to more than $50B.
- Free cash flow was $18.6B, down 27%, and gross margin slipped to about 67.8% from 69.05%. This is the bear case.
- OpenAI contributed about $10B of revenue, roughly 11% of the total. Microsoft owns about 24% of OpenAI.
- Anthropic committed at least $44.9B of Azure spend through 2033, per its S-1. Microsoft also holds an Anthropic stake.

**Price context**
- The stock ran to a record close of about $555.80 on Nov 4, a gain of roughly 6.7% that day. Sources attribute it to the midterm elections, and earlier to a roughly 18% post-earnings surge.
- It has since fallen to about $500, about 10% off the high. The 52-week range is roughly 349 to 559.
- The ex-dividend date is Nov 19 ($0.98). That is a small mechanical drop and not a catalyst.
- Analyst targets are about $610–636 on average, with a range of $440–870. Sentiment is Moderate Buy to Buy.
- TradingKey shows RSI at 40, Williams %R at 99 (oversold) and MACD at about -7.

**What to watch over the next 1–10 sessions**
- Nvidia earnings tonight.
- Anthropic's IPO pricing and first-day trading on Nov 18.
- Ignite, Nov 17–20. It is expected to push agents and Agent 365. I found no confirmed announcements yet.
- The post-incident report by Nov 20 and any customer-credit fallout.
- Whether software and IGV stabilize, and whether the roughly $500 round-number level holds.
- The next MSFT earnings date, Jan 27, is outside the window.

**Read**
- The setup is a sharp sector-driven pullback in a stock with strong fundamentals and no negative company news. Selling has followed the software complex and Anthropic headlines, which could continue or snap back quickly.
- The risks are an Anthropic-IPO "AI eats software" narrative, high yields, and a failure to hold $500.

agents.report:
CMC has had no company-specific bad news since its October earnings. The slide to 59.27 looks like a sector and macro de-rating on top of a soft earnings reaction. I found nothing dated Nov 12–17, so I can't tie today's move to a catalyst. Several sources are aggregators with inconsistent dates and prices, and I flag those below.

**Business and recent results**
- CMC makes rebar and merchant bar from scrap in electric-arc-furnace mills. It also owns a "Construction Solutions" segment (precast, Galvabar and downstream products) and a Europe steel segment.
- Fiscal Q4 (reported Oct 15) beat. Adjusted EPS was $2.09 against about $1.97 expected, and revenue was $2.658B, up 25.7%.
- Core EBITDA was $393.7M, with full-year core EBITDA of $1.36B against $837M a year earlier.
- North America Steel adjusted EBITDA was $317.5M, with a metal margin of $652/ton (up $84 year over year). Merchant bar volumes were up 27.5% and downstream backlog up 15.5%.
- Operating cash flow for the year was $1.06B, and adjusted net leverage was 1.9x.
- Source: [SEC 8-K earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000022444/000002244426000053/cmc-8312026xearningsreleas.htm).

**The negatives in the report** (per the [Earnings Whispers recap](https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/CMC/r111), a secondary source)
- Precast EBITDA was $57M, about $20M below what guidance implied. Weak Southeast residential activity, running at roughly 50–60% of normal, was blamed. Cumulative contribution since the acquisition was about $150M against a $165–175M target.
- The West Virginia micro mill is only starting hot commissioning, and the fiscal 2027 volume outlook was cut to under 200k tons from 250–300k.
- An unplanned Galvabar outage hurt Performance Reinforcing Steel. A second line is due later in calendar 2026.
- The low tax rate (about 7%) flattered Q4. Fiscal 2027 tax is guided to about 24%, which weighs on per-share growth.
- Q1 guidance: North America Steel EBITDA roughly flat sequentially, Construction Solutions down seasonally, Europe up (helped by a CO₂ credit).

**Positives and capital return**
- Run-rate savings from the TAG cost program exited the year above $250M against a $150M target, with another $100M targeted.
- Capex is guided to about $400M, down from roughly $580M.
- A $600M buyback increase on Aug 5 left about $702M of capacity. Per the Earnings Whispers recap, about $700M is to be pulled forward, though the actual pace is unconfirmed. Only $26.7M was bought in Q4.
- The quarterly dividend is $0.20 (ex-date Oct 28, paid Nov 11).
- Management calls fiscal 2027 "another strong year."

**Stock and analysts**
- The stock was about $65 before earnings and drifted lower afterward. One recap says shares fell 0.5% on the report, and another says they were down 9.8% from the June level.
- Analyst targets were trimmed on Oct 19: BMO to $73 (market perform) and Morgan Stanley to $84 (overweight). Goldman has a Buy at $85.
- Consensus is "Moderate Buy" (10 buy, 4 hold, 1 sell) with a $78.73 target. That is about 30% above the current price, which means little because targets lag the price.
- Source: [MarketBeat, Nov 12](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/consensus-commercial-metals-company-nyse-cmc-stock-has-average-price-target-of-7873-2026-11-12/). It showed an open of $64.77 on Nov 12, so the drop to about 59 came after that. Its 52-week low of $57.01 differs from your screen's 56.33. Its P/E was 11 and beta 1.55.
- The Earnings Whispers page header showed $59.45 with no timestamp.
- I found no insider trades.

**Other company news**
- On Nov 10 CMC announced that CFO Paul Lawrence will retire on Jan 15, 2027. Kenji Hashimoto (age 57) joined as Deputy CFO on Nov 16 and becomes CFO on Jan 15. The 8-K says there was no disagreement. It is a mild uncertainty ahead of the Jan 7 earnings date, not an alarm. Sources: [8-K exhibit](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000022444/000119312526454440/d175568dex991.htm) and [Stock Titan feed](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/CMC/).

**Sector and macro**
- On Nov 5 the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq 5.5% in an AI selloff, its worst day since April 2025. The trigger was fear that Democratic midterm wins could bring data-center moratoriums. That matters because CMC's story leans on data-center, chip-fab and infrastructure demand. Sources: [CP24/AP](https://www.cp24.com/news/money/2026/11/05/a-wipeout-for-ai-stocks-sends-wall-street-reeling-and-the-sp-500-tumbles-more-than-3/) and [KPTV](https://www.kptv.com/2026/11/05/brutal-sell-off-ai-stocks-sends-wall-street-reeling-sp-500-sees-worst-day-since-2025-liberation-day-tariffs/?outputType=apps).
- The same day steel stocks fell harder than the market: Steel Dynamics down 7.6%, Nucor down 8.3% and Cleveland-Cliffs down 12.2%, with no company news ([Trefis](https://www.trefis.com/stock/stld/articles2/623363/what-sent-steel-dynamics-stock-lower/2026-11-06)). Nucor had closed at a 2026 high of $277.65 on Nov 2 and was at $245.68 after the drop. Steel peers fell about 1% on Oct 15 on tariff doubts ([24/7 Wall St](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/15/cleveland-cliffs-drops-4-as-tariff-doubt-returns-nucor-and-steel-dynamics-slip/)). I found no data on how they traded Nov 6–17.
- Tariffs: Section 232 steel duties are at 50% and U.S. steel imports are running about 30% below last year (secondary sources). There are reports of possible tariff relief for Canada, and U.S.-Canada trade talks have swung back and forth. Tariff-deal headlines have hit steel stocks before ([Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/international-trade/us-steel-stocks-fall-on-speculation-over-import-tariff-deals), [Stocktwits](https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/nue-stld-cenx-clf-stocks-slide-as-trump-halves-import-tariff-on-canadian-steel-and-aluminum/cZYduaiRJlA)). I couldn't date those items.
- Rebar trade cases: Commerce made final affirmative antidumping and countervailing duty determinations in 2026 against Algeria (127% dumping margin), Bulgaria (53%), Egypt and Vietnam (about 123–132% antidumping plus 6.8% countervailing). That is a multi-year protection tailwind for CMC. Management flagged South Korean imports as a concern on the June call. Sources: [SteelOrbis, Egypt](https://www.steelorbis.com/steel-news/latest-news/us-issues-final-ad-and-cvd-determinations-on-rebar-from-egypt-1469870.htm) and [SteelOrbis, Bulgaria](https://www.steelorbis.com/steel-news/latest-news/us-issues-final-ad-determination-on-rebar-from-bulgaria-1470106.htm). I couldn't confirm the ITC final votes.
- Pricing: one result says Nucor announced a $30/ton rebar increase for orders after Nov 7, and Gerdau matched it, taking the base price to $895/t. The article had no year, so treat it as unconfirmed. If it is 2026, it is a supportive margin signal. The company said scrap was a margin headwind (war-related fuel costs), but another source said ample scrap supply was easing mill costs in early November.
- China rebar prices are soft (seasonal off-season), which has little direct effect on CMC.

**Interpretation for a 1–10 session decision**
- Bear case: the stock is breaking a 20-day low, sits below falling 50- and 200-day averages, and is about 5% above its 52-week low. Selling has outrun the news, and it is high-beta and tied to the AI/data-center narrative that cracked on Nov 5. Soft precast and a delayed West Virginia ramp cap near-term estimates, and flat Q1 guidance gives no catalyst until Jan 7. Sector tariff headlines can hit it again.
- Bull case: earnings and cash flow were strong, valuation is about 11x earnings, and buybacks are being pulled forward. A fresh rebar price increase and trade protection support margins. A sector mean-reversion bounce is plausible after the Nov 5 flush.
- Nothing I found explains today's -0.3% on 2.1x volume. It reads as continued distribution within a sector downtrend, with no new fundamental catalyst.

**Gaps**
- I couldn't find a transcript of the Oct 15 call or any dated news from Nov 12–17.
- I found no information on short interest or on how the sector or index traded this week.

# HGV research as of 12:10 PM CT, Tuesday 2026-11-17

I did not find any news from the last week that explains the move. I couldn't read the Q3 call transcript (the PDF wouldn't parse), so what management said on the call is not covered.

## The story
HGV is a Hilton-branded timeshare company. It sells vacation points, mostly to existing owners, and earns money from financing the loans. It also owns 51% of Bluegreen and Big Cedar. It carries heavy debt: $4.9B corporate debt at 5.75%, $2.9B non-recourse debt, and net leverage of about 3.9x.

The stock fell from about 55 to the mid-30s over 2026. The Q3 print on Oct 29 set a low bar:
- **Contract sales:** $807M, down 11%. Value per guest (VPG, sales per tour) fell 12.5% while tour flow rose 1.7%.
- **Guidance cut:** Full-year adjusted EBITDA (excluding deferrals and recognitions) dropped to $1.165-1.18B from $1.225-1.265B.
- **Cause:** Management blames leadership changes and lost salespeople in key markets. Q2 contract sales were already down 3%, and Q3 was flagged as likely worse. CEO Mark Wang said he was "not satisfied" but saw "initial signs of progress" exiting the quarter. A Yahoo-hosted fund letter says the fix is slower than hoped. Mike Riley was promoted to chief sales and marketing officer.
- **Headline EPS is distorted:** Adjusted EPS of $4.03 against about $1.08 expected includes a $296M ($3.76 per share) construction recognition on a Hawaii project. The release does not tie it to Ka Haku. A $55M cut to the loan-loss allowance also boosted revenue. Ignore the "beat."
- **Cash flow and buyback:** Q3 free cash flow was $52M and nine-month free cash flow was $273M, versus $29M a year ago. On Oct 30, HGV launched a $200M accelerated share repurchase (ASR) with Deutsche Bank, priced off the $35.71 close on Oct 29. It received about 4.48M shares up front, with final settlement by Dec 31. About $417M of authorization remains afterward.

## Why the stock is up
- **Price path:** It closed 35.71 on Oct 29 and is now 45.57, up about 28%.
- **Day one:** It rose about 6.7% on Oct 30.
- **Gap-up and consolidation:** It was 41.29 on Nov 3, 44.62-44.66 on Nov 9-10, about 43.8 on Nov 13, and 45.57 now.
- **Why:** The best explanation I found is relief after expectations were reset, plus the ASR (CFO: "confidence in the strength of our underlying business"). A Kalkine piece says the same, but I could not open it.
- **Insider buys:** CEO Wang bought 12,200 shares at 40.92 on Nov 2, about $499K. A director bought 2,500 at 41.55. Those buys came after a large Wang option-exercise sale at about $51.93 in May. A different executive, Corbin, sold 60,401 shares at 43.41 on Nov 4 under a pre-arranged 10b5-1 plan.
- **Peer read-through:** Marriott Vacations (VAC) reported Nov 4 with contract sales up 29% and VPG up 30%. It nudged guidance up, and the stock was about 115 on Nov 13. That supports the idea that timeshare demand isn't broken industry-wide, so HGV's problem looks company-specific. VAC also flagged gas prices and interest rates as consumer risks, and its Oct securitization priced at 5.91% versus 4.86% in April.
- **Short covering is possible but unproven:** Short interest was 13.9M shares, or 19% of shares, at Oct 30. That was up 82% from Oct 15, with about 11 days to cover. I have no data after Oct 30, so whether shorts have been squeezed since is unknown.

## Analysts

**AA research as of 12:10 PM CT, Tue 2026-11-17. I found no AA-specific news today or this week.**

The weakness looks like the sector and the market, not a company event. The fundamentals are fine today, but the aluminum cycle is turning down. Several of the secondary sites I used (Discovery Alert, Tickeron, Tradestie, Kedia) are low-reliability. I marked their figures as unverified where they matter.

**How we got here**
- The 2026 run-up came from the Middle East war and Hormuz disruption, which cut Gulf smelter output. Gulf smelters were about 9% of global primary aluminum supply, and some, such as EGA, took physical damage. LME 3-month aluminum peaked near $3,800 in June.
- AA hit a 52-week high near $84 in late May to early June, then fell about 50%. Hormuz passage eased, Gulf smelters reconnected to markets, and Chinese and Indonesian output filled the gap. Wells Fargo, for example, cut its target to $71 from $82 in that period.
- Alcoa announced the $4.1B South32 (AliGroup) acquisition earlier this year, and the stock fell about 9% to $47.41 on dilution and financing worries. Terms:
  - About $3.1B in cash.
  - About 17M Alcoa shares, roughly 6% dilution.
  - Up to $750M contingent on prices.
  - About $900M of targeted synergies.
  - South32 shareholders approved on Oct 15; closing is expected in the first half of 2027.
- Pinjarra refinery instability caused a Q2 miss and a cut to 2026 alumina guidance.

**Q3, reported Oct 15 (company release)**
- Adjusted EPS was $1.82 against a consensus of about $1.51, a beat. Revenue was $3.70B, slightly below the $3.77B estimate.
- Adjusted EBITDA was $789M, down $112M from Q2.
- Aluminum segment EBITDA fell to $862M from a record $1,073M. The realized price was $4,527/t against $4,752/t, and adjusted operating cost rose to $2,584/t from $2,481/t.
- Alumina segment EBITDA recovered to about -$1M from -$96M as Pinjarra stabilized. Output rose 11% sequentially.
- Operating cash flow was $643M and free cash flow $472M. Cash was $4.4B, including about $2.6B of acquisition bonds issued Sept 23 at 6.625% and 6.875%. Net debt was $414M and total debt $4.8B. The bridge facility was cancelled.
- The Q4 outlook is a drag: about $30M worse in Aluminum from raw materials and maintenance, about $30M more in alumina input costs, and alumina EBITDA roughly flat. Interest expense is about $185M for 2026.
- The 2026 production and shipment guidance was reaffirmed.
- Massena East, an idle site in New York, is being sold for a data center. Potential proceeds are up to $315M, with $50M to $65M at closing. It is the first step toward a $0.5B to $1B asset-monetization goal by 2030.

**The stock after earnings**
- It rose about 5% to 8% the next morning, then reversed.
- On Oct 22, Argus cut it to Hold, citing pricing pressure, supply growth outside the Middle East, tariffs and competitor expansion. The stock fell more than 5% that day at one point. Argus puts forward earnings at about 6x.
- Target cuts followed:
  - Oct 7: Morgan Stanley (Equal Weight, $50) and JPMorgan (Neutral, $50).
  - Oct 16: Wells Fargo to $58 from $60.
  - Oct 20: B. Riley to $63 from $80 (Buy), Citi to $56 from $76 (Buy), and Freedom Broker to $62 from $76 (Buy).
- Consensus is Hold at about $55 to $60, with 7 Buy, 5 Hold and 1 Sell. The stock is far below every target.
- The stock fell 4.4% to about $39.98 on Nov 10. It closed at $39.74 on Nov 13 and about $39.25 on Nov 16. That means today's $37.39 is a further drop of roughly 4.7%, about 3.3% on the day by your screen. The Nov 10 drop was reported in a headline, but I couldn't open the article to see its cause.
- Insider sales in late August at about $51 were small. There was no recent insider buying that I found.

**Aluminum market now**
- LME 3-month aluminum is about $3,010 to $3,020/t, roughly 20% below the June high.
- The physical market is unusually tight:
  - LME stocks are about 224,000 to 226,000 t, the lowest since 1990 and down about 56% this year.
  - The cash-to-3-month backwardation hit about $177/t on Nov 12, reported as the widest since 1990, and eased to about $131 by Nov 16.
  - Trafigura holds large November positions. The November contract expires this week, which creates short-squeeze risk in the nearby contract.
- The forward view is bearish, though:
  - Goldman sees a surplus of 1.5 Mt in 2026 and 2 Mt in 2027, with Indonesian output doubling.
  - Morgan Stanley sees 0.83 Mt in 2027, Macquarie about 0.39 Mt, and Citi 1.8 Mt in 2027.
  - EGA has restarted 61% of its Al Taweelah cells, though further restarts are expected to be gradual.
  - China's exports are up 18% this year.
  - Chinese aluminum-processing demand is soft (PMI 48.9).
- The US Section 232 tariff is still 50%, and the Midwest premium is about $1.12/lb, down from a record $1.19/lb in May. This premium is a large part of Alcoa's US pricing, so its trend matters for AA.
- Peer Century Aluminum (CENX) is also weak, near its 52-week lows at about $32 to $34. It missed Q3 adjusted EPS ($2.58 against $2.75), and UBS cut its target.

**Macro today**
- The S&P 500 fell about 1.9% on Monday, led by chips, and was down roughly 0.7% to 1% on Tuesday ahead of Nvidia earnings after the close.
- A December Fed hike is almost fully priced in, and a St. Louis Fed president (Musalem) said more hikes may come sooner. The dollar is near 19-month highs. These are headwinds for commodities.
- Materials were reported as an early relative leader this morning, so AA's weakness is stock-specific or aluminum-specific.

**For the 1 to 10 session decision**
- **Bearish:** The trend is firmly down. The stock sits below its falling 50-day and 200-day averages, and the aluminum 2027 surplus narrative is spreading. Rate-hike and dollar pressure continue, and the Q4 cost headwinds are known. AA is a high-beta stock (beta about 1.74) and tends to follow the market down on risk-off days.
- **Bullish:** The stock is cheap, at about 6x to 7x earnings. Cash flow is strong, net debt is low, and the analyst targets are well above the price. Physical tightness could produce a squeeze or a snap-back rally. The price is also close to the 52-week low of about $35, which is a nearby support test.
- **Open question:** I found no catalyst that explains today's drop, so it may be an elevated-volume breakdown continuation.
- **Near-term catalysts to watch:**
  - The LME November expiry this week.
  - Nvidia's results tonight.
  - Any Midwest premium or tariff changes.
  - The Massena sale closing and the AliGroup regulatory approvals.
  - Q4 earnings are not until Jan 21, so there is no earnings risk in the window.

**Why it has been weak**
- BioPharma Dive on Oct 9 said XBI "steadily lost value" after August and "traded sideways" (Cantor).

- Biotech M&A is strong but concentrated in private companies. Private deals have already beaten the combined totals of the prior eight years.
- Public-company buyouts have been light, and RBC says dealmaking often rebounds after the slow July to September stretch. A pickup in public deals is a possible upside catalyst.
- Recent deals I found: Lilly buying Merida for up to $2.9B, and AbbVie licensing Gilgamesh's bretisilocin for up to $1.2B (dated Nov 8). The Lilly announcement date is unconfirmed.

  - Spyre was -5.6%.
  - Oruka was -3.4%.

**COF research summary, as of 12:10 PM CT on 2026-11-17**

I found no single news item that explains today's 2.8% drop. The pieces I did find point to a slow slide from macro and political overhangs, not a company-specific shock. Some figures come from secondary sites and conflict across sources, so I've flagged those.

**Where the stock stands**
- The Motley Fool page shows COF at $187.91, down 2.75% at 12:49 PM ET today, which matches your screen. The prior close was about $193.2 to $193.6.
- The stock opened 2026 at about $242.52 and is down roughly 16 to 20% for the year.
- The 52-week range is roughly $174 to $260. Sources differ slightly; your screen has $172.91 to $255.59.
- The Q3 earnings pop faded. Shares rose about 4% on Oct 20 and 21 and then gave it back, which Simply Wall St described as the stock "shrugging off" the beat.
- Market cap is about $116B and the dividend yield is about 2.1%.

**Q3 2026 results (reported Oct 20)**
- Adjusted EPS was $6.69 against an estimate of about $5.50. GAAP EPS was $5.61 and net income $3.5B. Revenue was $16.3B, up 6%, roughly in line.
- Credit improved. The domestic card charge-off rate was 3.98%, down 73 bps from Q2 and 65 bps year over year. Management called credit "in a very good place."
- The card delinquency rate rose to 3.74% from 3.39% in Q2 but was down from 3.89% a year earlier. Management attributed the rise to normal seasonality.
- Auto charge-offs rose to 1.59%, and auto delinquency was 4.64%.
- The quarter included a $225M allowance release, which bears say flattered earnings.
- Card purchase volume rose 11% to nearly $255B, helped by moving debit cards onto the Discover network. Consumer banking revenue rose 17%, and auto originations rose 22%.
- CET1 capital was 13.8%, and the company bought back $2.6B of stock.
- Discover synergies reached $1.8B annualized. Integration costs have passed $2.8B, with $338M in Q3, and are expected to end by 2028.
- Marketing was $1.6B, up 14%. Management said Q4 marketing would step up, and Fairbank said the premium card business is "very marketing-intensive." Domestic card expenses rose 9% year over year, driven by technology, marketing and Brex.
- Discover card loans shrank about 3% year over year, with more contraction expected. Deposits fell 1% from Q2. Liquidity reserves fell $10B to about $134B.
- The Visa/Mastercard interchange settlement will cut interchange revenue. Management said the impact is about equal to the remaining synergies and called its estimate uncertain, with a "wide error bar."
- Management declined to guide on the efficiency ratio. Analysts pressed on whether marketing will erode the Discover earnings power and whether card credit can keep improving.

**Strategy and corporate**
- The Brex acquisition ($5.15B, announced January) closed April 7, 2026.
- Discover accounts began migrating onto Capital One's platform on July 27, 2026, a process expected to run through 2027.
- Capital One is also moving debit cards, and some new credit cards, onto the Discover network. Existing credit cards have no disclosed timeline.
- A Simply Wall St piece dated Nov 16 mentions recent online banking outages. It calls the impact "more reputational than financial" and gives no dates, cause or price move.

**Political and regulatory overhang (the likeliest driver of November weakness)**
- Trump called for a 10% credit card rate cap on Jan 12. COF fell about 6% intraday that day and card stocks fell 8 to 11%. Experts say there is no clear executive authority without legislation.
- On Nov 4, after Democrats won both chambers of Congress, COF, Synchrony and Bread fell 3.5 to 4.3%. TD Cowen said a rate cap became more likely, and Jaret Seiberg said any cap could land nearer 36% than 10%.
- The Credit Card Competition Act was reintroduced in January with Trump's support. Attempts to attach it to the GENIUS Act and a housing bill failed, and I found no floor vote.
- The Visa/Mastercard $38B merchant settlement got preliminary approval in June. Final approval is pending, with the National Retail Federation (NRF) and others opposed and a possible appeal to the 2nd Circuit.

**Macro**
- The Fed raised rates 25 bps to 3.75 to 4.00% on Sep 16 and held on Oct 28 in a 10-2 vote. Cook and Hammack dissented in favor of another hike.
- The Fool article notes loan growth could slow as rates rise. The Fed has scaled back its meeting schedule, but I did not confirm the next meeting date.
- I found no market wrap for today, so I can't say whether this is a sector or market-wide move.

**Analysts**
- The consensus rating is Moderate Buy. MarketBeat counts 20 buys and 4 holds among 24 analysts, and the average target is about $256.
- Recent moves were mostly target trims, with no rating changes in November:
  - Redburn cut to $260 from $275 around Nov 13.
  - UBS cut to $274 from $280 on Nov 2, keeping its Buy.
  - Piper Sandler raised to $269 on Oct 21.
  - The ad-hoc-news site listed Morgan Stanley at $267 and JPMorgan at $227. I did not verify these.
- Targets sit 30 to 40% above the current price, which shows how far sentiment has detached from analysts.

**Next earnings and gaps**
- Next earnings are 2027-01-19, outside the 1 to 10 session window. Monthly credit metrics, usually released mid-month, may be a catalyst. I did not verify their timing.
- I could not find today's news driver, short interest or insider activity (MarketBeat blocked the fetch), or any COF-specific November event beyond the outage mention.

**Read for a 1 to 10 session trade**
- Bearish: the stock is below both moving averages, near the lows, and falling on elevated volume. The rate-cap, Credit Card Competition Act and Congress headlines are unresolved, and the Fed is leaning hawkish.
- Bullish: credit is improving, buybacks are heavy, valuation looks depressed against consensus targets, and the fundamental thesis is intact. A bounce is plausible if the selling is sector-wide.
- Policy headline risk cuts both ways in the short run. The stock fell 6% on the rate-cap news in January and 3.5 to 4% after the Democratic win.

The source detail below is thin in places, and several of the macro and AI claims come from one bullish newsletter that I could not cross-check.

**What URA is**

  - NexGen is 6.3%.
  - Kazatomprom is 5.4%.
  - Oklo is 4.7%.
  - Uranium Energy Corp is 4.0%.
  - Paladin is 2.9%.
- The index also includes nuclear components, so URA trades partly as an AI-power and reactor basket. That is a different driver from the uranium price.

**Why it is down**
1. **The AI and tech unwind is spilling into nuclear.** Today the Nasdaq is down about 1.6%, the S&P 500 about 1.3%, and the VIX is near 26. Nvidia reports after the close, its first report without Jensen Huang as CEO, and the stock is down about 26% in a month. Cameco and the nuclear names have traded with AI-power stocks. A Yahoo piece says Cameco rose 6% on Nov 9, when Constellation jumped 10%, and then gave it all back.
2. **Rates and inflation.**
   - The 10-year yield is about 5.09%.
   - A St. Louis Fed president said more hikes are likely.
   - The uranium newsletter cites a hot October CPI and a likely December hike.
   - Capital-heavy miners are hurt by this.
3. **Company-specific misses.**
   - Cameco's Q3 was weak:
     - It posted an adjusted loss of C$2M.
     - Production fell 20% because of a Key Lake mill shutdown.
     - Cash cost per pound rose 62%.
     - Analysts cut 2026 EPS estimates.
     - The stock hit a 52-week low on Monday, with no news that day.
   - Paladin's Q1 cost was $61.60/lb against $44–48 guidance. The newsletter says it fell 17.6% on Nov 13, but I could not confirm that.
   - Ur-Energy reportedly fell 16% on Nov 10 (newsletter only).
4. **Supply of Cameco shares.** On Nov 5 Cameco doubled its at-the-market equity program to US$1B, about 3.5% of its market value. That could cap rebounds.
5. **Nuclear-name volatility.**
   - Nuclear stocks bounced hard on Nov 6 (Oklo up about 23%, Centrus up 17%).

I made no trades and wrote no files. The sources are mostly news sites and aggregators. A few of the biggest ones (Benzinga, CNBC) refused to open, so I relied on their search summaries. Treat the exact figures as approximate.

**Bottom line:** XLK is oversold in the middle of a three-way event cluster. The first event is Nvidia earnings after today's close. The second is the Anthropic IPO, which is expected to price tomorrow and start trading Thursday. The third is the Trump–Xi meeting, set for Thursday. The 20-day-low break and RSI 33 say little next to a gap risk from Nvidia (about 13% of XLK) that tonight's report could drive in either direction.

**How the slide happened**
- **Nov 5:** XLK fell 8.04%, its worst day since March 2020, on about 3 times normal volume. Reported cause: fear that AI data-center buildout will slow after the midterm elections. Voters passed state measures to slow data-center construction.
  - Nvidia fell more than 9% that day, and the Nasdaq fell about 5.5%.
  - The VIX had its biggest one-day jump since April 2025.
- **Nov 8–12:** Nvidia's board opened an investigation into reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. Huang then admitted an affair and resigned on Nov 12. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO.
- **Nov 16:** XLK fell 3.24%, the weakest sector by a wide margin. A Commerce Department rule closed the loophole that let Chinese firms rent Nvidia computing from third-country data centers. It requires licenses for chip shipments to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil.
  - A semiconductor ETF fell about 4.7%, and Micron fell as much as 7%.
  - Nvidia closed at $156.10, its lowest close since June 2025, after six straight weekly losses.
- **Nov 17 (today):** Software is leading the drop.
  - Salesforce is down about 9.7%, Intuit about 6.7%, Microsoft about 3%, and a software ETF about 4.4%.
  - Anthropic launched office tools, which feeds the fear that AI will erode per-seat software subscriptions. Some commentators also say funds are selling software to make room for the IPO. One source says there is no proof of that.
  - Nvidia is roughly flat to down 1.5%. Huang said he would return as CEO if asked. CNBC reports the board isn't considering it.
- **Market tone:** The S&P 500 is down about 1.2% and the Nasdaq about 1.2–1.6%. The VIX is about 25.9.

**Macro backdrop**
- The Fed under Chair Warsh hiked in September. The funds rate is 3.75–4%, and markets price a December hike at roughly 72–84%. St. Louis Fed President Musalem said today that 100–150 basis points more may be needed.
- The 10-year yield is about 5.1%, up from about 4.45% in June. Higher rates hurt debt-funded data-center builders, and CoreWeave and Nebius are reported down about 45% in a month.
- Fed official Goolsbee called the AI buildout "old-fashioned overheating."
- October retail sales were a little better than expected, up 0.2%. Homebuilder sentiment is at its lowest since 2012.

  - Nvidia is down about 35% from its October high, a loss of roughly $2T.

  - Nigam Arora (Arora Report) sees longer-term downside risk unless a strong new CEO is found.

**XLK's makeup and valuation**
- Apple is about 16.5%, Nvidia 12.6–13.8%, Microsoft 12–13%, and Broadcom about 5%. The top 10 are about 65%, so Nvidia and Microsoft earnings and news dominate the fund. Software sits inside XLK, so today's software drop hits it directly.

**QUBT: research for the 1–10 session decision (as of 12:10 PM CT, Tuesday 2026-11-17)**

**Bottom line:** I found no company-specific negative news behind the slide. It looks like a high-beta sector selloff, with QUBT dragged along by the quantum group. The stock trades near or below its reported cash, which gives it a real valuation floor argument. The business itself is weak: acquired revenue, a 4.5% gross margin and rising losses. Nothing in my search shows the selling is finished.

**What the stock is doing**
- Monday's close was $5.25, down 5.6%, and today it is near $5.05 (a 24/7 Wall St. snapshot showed $5.06, down 3.7%).
- The prior 52-week low was cited as $5.18. Today's price is below that, so this is a fresh multi-year-style low in this window, not a bounce off support.
- It fell about 31% over three months. Before the Nov 9 report it was around $6.3–6.9. It rose 8.4% to $6.86 on earnings day, then gave all of that back and more within about five sessions. The beta is cited at about 3.95.
- The 50-day is about $7.3 and the 200-day about $8.5.

**Why the sector is falling (all sector-wide)**
- **Rates:** October CPI came in hot at +0.4% versus +0.3% expected (TipRanks, Nov 12). The 10-year yield rose from 4.98% on Nov 10 to 5.15% on Nov 13. Some coverage mentions rate-hike expectations.
- **Tech and AI risk-off:** Nvidia weakness and nerves ahead of its earnings report. The Nasdaq 100 fell 1.16% on the day of the 247wallst piece.
- **Peers' results:**
  - Rigetti: revenue was $1.4M.
  - D-Wave: revenue was +21% but bookings were down 19%, and the stock fell on that. A retiring CFO was also mentioned.
  - IonQ: revenue was up 336% and the stock still fell.
- **Dilution fear:**
  - IonQ priced a $2B equity offering on Oct 14.
  - Wedbush attributes the group's 25–40% decline since late September to share sales and back-loaded revenue. Wedbush remains confident in the technology. I could only find this secondhand, not in a Wedbush note.
  - 247wallst says investors are "pricing in funding and dilution risk."

**QUBT's own story**
- **Q3 (reported Nov 9):**
  - Revenue was $9.5M, up from $384K a year earlier, against estimates of about $7.6M. It was larger than all of the first half of 2026 combined and up about 71% from Q2's $5.55M.
  - The growth came mostly from acquisitions: Luminar Semiconductor (closed Feb 2, 2026 for $110M cash), NuCrypt and NHanced. The report does not split organic from acquired revenue.
  - Gross margin was 4.5% ($428K gross profit).
  - Operating expenses were $29M, up from $10.5M, and management called about $29M a quarter a reasonable run rate. Headcount is above 330.
  - The net loss was $15.1M, or $0.07 a share, against an expected $0.04 loss. Interest income of about $13M cushions it.
- **Cash:**
  - About $1.3B in cash and investments, of which $174M is cash and about $1.1B is investments. This is mostly from the 2025 private placements, which raised about $1.45–1.64B.
  - Market caps cited were $1.19B (MarketBeat, at about $5.25) and about $1.55B (Insider Monkey, earlier). On either figure the stock trades near or below its cash.
  - Management says liquidity covers at least 12 months and it prefers to avoid dilutive raises. It plans $70–80M of capex for Fab 2, mostly through March 2027, and continues to look at M&A.
  - Cash burn is modest relative to the $1.3B. The main risk is cash being spent on more acquisitions.
- **Backlog and guidance:**
  - Backlog is $39.1M, slightly down from the prior quarter. About 70% is aerospace and government, mostly subcontracts.
  - There is no formal guidance. Management expects a "strong finish" to 2026 and lumpy results.
- **Product:**
  - Dirac-3S (up to 9,980 variables, announced Oct 1) is due to make its first customer shipment in Q4 2026. Management's own benchmarks showed it comparable to or weaker than rivals on some problems.
  - There is an INmune Bio commercial deal (the first drug-industry customer) and a partnership with Hamad Bin Khalifa University in Qatar.
  - Export and ITAR limits hold back overseas sales.
- **Leadership:** Dr. Yuping Huang was confirmed as CEO in December 2025, after Dr. William McGann retired.
- **Short interest:**
  - The latest figure I found was 64.7M shares, with 8.9 days to cover, from the 2026-09-18 settlement (equibles). Curved Trading lists the same 64.7M shares for 2026-07-15, so the dating is unclear. I found nothing newer.
  - It is large against roughly 226M shares outstanding (my estimate from market cap and price, not a reported figure).
  - That cuts both ways: squeeze potential on a bounce, but also evidence that shorts have been right.
- **Institutional ownership** is cited at only 4.3%.

**Analysts (nothing new since the earnings reaction)**
- Wedbush reaffirmed Neutral on Nov 10.
- Rosenblatt reiterated Buy with a $22 target on Oct 19.
- Cantor has Neutral with a $10 target (Aug).
- Ascendiant has Buy with a $32 target.
- Northland has Buy with a $20 target.
- Consensus is about Hold, with an average target of about $19. Some feeds say Strong Buy with a $23 target.
- Wall Street Zen cut it to Strong Sell on Nov 14, which is a quant rating and not meaningful.
- I found no downgrade or new note since earnings.

**Catalysts in the 1–10 session window**

- **Macro:** Rate and yield moves, and the next inflation prints.
- **Dirac-3S:** A first-shipment announcement is possible any time in Q4, which would be a small positive.
- **Filings:** Form 4s and 8-Ks for any financing or acquisition.
- **Sector news:** Any further quantum share sales. Anything in the group that makes people think QUBT might also raise money would hurt, although it already holds $1.3B.

   - Treasury yields are high: 10-year about 5.12%, 30-year about 5.47%, 2-year about 4.81%. Import prices rose 1.1% against a 0.7% forecast.
   - Long-duration, unprofitable growth stocks like ARKK's are the most exposed to this.
   - The Fed's October meeting minutes come out Wednesday, 11/18.
2. **An AI-infrastructure scare.**
   - On 11/5 the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.5% and the S&P 500 fell 4.4%, the worst day since April 2025. The trigger was fear that the Democratic midterm win would slow data-center buildout, plus credit stress at AI cloud providers (CoreWeave credit spreads hit a record).

3. **Nvidia and other tech headlines.**
   - Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO, and Colette Kress is interim. Nvidia is down nearly 24% in November.
   - A reported classified NSA network outage added to the pressure on the major averages.
   - Microsoft fell about 3%, Micron about 6%, Intel about 4%, and CoreWeave, Iren and Nebius 4-6%.
4. **Crypto-linked holdings are weak.**
   - Coinbase and Circle are far below their highs. Binance disclosed a roughly $6.3B hack on 10/30, and Coinbase fell about 12% that day.
   - Bitcoin is around $63-64k, down from about $76k on 11/5.

**What ARK is doing**
- **11/5:** ARK bought Nvidia ($45.9M), AMD ($19.8M), SpaceX ($48.7M) and Coinbase. It was buying the dip.

agents.report:
**BILL (BILL Holdings): research as of 12:10 PM CT, Tue 2026-11-17**

**Why it's up today.** The move is a deal rumor, not fundamentals.
- The Financial Times reported that TPG (a large private equity firm) is nearing an agreement to take BILL private. It cited unnamed sources. Investing.com's write-up was posted at 11:46 AM on Nov 17, and Seeking Alpha's version said the same.
- The FT said the deal would come at a premium and could be finalized "in the coming days." It also said timing could shift and talks could collapse.
- No price per share has been reported. TPG declined to comment, and BILL had not responded. I found no press release, 8-K or confirmation from either side.
- Both articles put the early reaction at about +8% and cite a $4.8B market value. Your screen shows +9.2% at about $62.94, and Investing.com's ticker showed about +10%.

**The move began before the report.** On Mon Nov 16, William Blair upgraded BILL from Market Perform to Outperform and the stock rose about 5.2%. The analyst, Andrew Jeffrey, cited these points:
- Margin expansion beyond what guidance reflects, helped by a headcount cut of more than 30%.
- Improving monetization, with ad valorem product adoption growing in the high teens.
- Estimates above consensus: FY28 EBIT about 10% above.
- He called the upgrade "tactical," and he named competitors (Corpay, Fiserv, Stripe) and low barriers to entry as risks.

That helps explain the +17% over five sessions, the new 52-week high and the RSI of 83. The upgrade is the only identified catalyst before today.

**The sale story is not new.**
- **Activists:** Starboard held 8.5% and nominated four directors in September 2025. It settled on Oct 15, 2025, with Peter Feld and Lee Kirkpatrick joining the board. Elliott (at least 5%) and Barington (urging a sale) were also involved.
- **Earlier sale reports:**
  - Reuters, Nov 2025: BILL was exploring a sale.
  - Bloomberg, Feb 6, 2026: Hellman & Friedman (another large private equity firm) was in talks to buy BILL, with other private equity suitors also interested.
  - Stock reaction in Feb 2026: up about 21% on Feb 6 on the earnings beat, and about 32% on the day by one source's count. It closed at $47.02.
  - Truist estimated a takeout value of $59–$70 per share.
- **What happened to H&F:** I found no report of a deal or of talks ending. The stock then drifted to about $44 on average (BILL's average buyback price in the September quarter). That suggests the Feb process did not produce a deal.
- **Management:** The CEO has said BILL is "always evaluating" M&A. The Q1 call transcript I read did not address a sale or strategic review.

**Fundamentals (FQ1 2027, reported Nov 5).**
- **Revenue:** $353.8M total, up 13%. Core revenue was $316.4M, up 14%. Revenue is now reported net of rewards, a presentation change only.
- **Profitability:** Non-GAAP operating income was $136.9M against an outlook of $112.5M, a 39% margin. GAAP net income was $60.3M versus a $3.0M loss a year earlier. Rule of 40 was 51.
- **Buyback:** About $300M repurchased at an average of about $44.18 per share.
- **Guidance:**
  - FY27 total revenue is $1.43–1.46B, about 10–12% growth.
  - FY27 non-GAAP operating margin is about 33%.
  - FY27 non-GAAP EPS is $3.99–4.15.
  - Management says the restructuring is "not done" and that Q1's low spending is not a new baseline.
- **Valuation at $62.94:** about 15–16x FY27 non-GAAP EPS (my calculation).

**Setup for a 1–10 session decision.**
- **If a deal is announced:** The price becomes pinned near the offer. The upside is likely modest unless the offer is well above today's price. Analyst estimates from Feb ($59–70) put today's price in the middle of that range, so a bid near the low end is plausible.
- **If talks collapse or drag on:** The risk is a sharp give-back. Much of the five-session gain (about $9, from roughly $54) rests on rumor. The pre-rumor level was about $57–58 after the upgrade.
- **Other considerations:**
  - A prior sale process (Feb 2026) ended without a deal, which is a precedent for rumors that don't close.
  - SPY is down 1.2% today and BILL is strong against it, which fits the volume and the deal bid.

**Caveats.** Search results had inconsistent dates and prices (for example, a "52-week high of $58.35" and a "$55.25" price from earlier snapshots). I could not open the FT, Bloomberg or the Q1 press release directly, and the Benzinga transcript returned 403. The call details come from the Webull transcript, which is auto-generated and may contain errors. I did not find a Nov 17 filing from BILL, TPG or the SEC.

**Drone and defense-tech basket, 12:10 PM CT, Tuesday 2026-11-17**

I ran about 11 searches and opened 4 pages. Late searches mostly repeated earlier results. The last few turned up nothing new on the Ukraine ceasefire status, on AVAV's next earnings date, or on a company response to the AEVEX lawsuit. I read the full article for RCAT, ONDS and AEVEX only. I did not open the KTOS, UMAC or AVAV pages, so those rest on search summaries. Some sources disagree on figures, noted below.

**The story in one line**

Today's -6.9% is mostly one name. RCAT fell about 33% on a revenue disaster that looks company-specific. It sits on top of a sector that has been falling for weeks on growth-stock weakness, "defense peak" worries and ceasefire hopes. The five other names are down far less today. In the morning snapshot, ONDS was about -5%, AVAV -0.8% to -3.5%, and KTOS -0.7%. AVEX is up 2.2% in your screen.

**Today's catalyst: RCAT**
- Fiscal Q3 revenue was $11.77M against about $40.7M expected, a miss of roughly 70%. It still grew 22% year over year.
- Gross profit was only $65K. Operating expenses were $43.5M and net loss was $40.5M.
- Management withdrew the full-year 2026 revenue target, which had been reaffirmed in August, and gave no replacement.
- It blamed slow contract awards, a weak result in the Pentagon's Drone Dominance "Gauntlet II" evaluation, and poor visibility on procurement timing.
- Cash is $242.7M, but the company burned $156.8M in operations over nine months. Shares outstanding rose to about 152.8M from 99.6M. A Steyr Motors acquisition is pending.
- Needham cut its target but stayed positive on 2027. I did not find the new target.
- The stock was about $2.32 to $2.39 this morning, near -71% year to date. It was $3.60 on Nov 16, after a 5% drop that day.
- The sources call it the worst session in over 5 years, since June 2021.
- Peers barely reacted, which fits a company-specific event.

**Why the whole group is weak**
- Nov 16: Nasdaq 100 fell 1.4% on an AI and growth selloff. The small, high-beta drone names took some of the biggest hits (ONDS -8%, RCAT -5%, UMAC -4%).
- Ondas fell 9% on Nov 10, 5% on Nov 12 (despite record revenue and a raised outlook), and 6% on Oct 14. "Good news, stock falls" has been the pattern.
- Ukraine ceasefire expectations and talk of a defense-sector cyclical peak are weighing on defense stocks. Czech arms maker CSG hit a record low today, down about 72% since its January IPO.
- A CNBC piece says South Korean defense stocks are in a sharp selloff. I found nothing current on the status of the ceasefire talks themselves.
- The Drone Dominance program (a roughly $1.1B push to buy 200,000+ drones by 2027) is real, but Gauntlet II winners were other firms: Perennial Autonomy won Deep Strike and Neros won Close Quarters, with a Neros order of $100M+. Red Cat was not among the leaders I found. Production and a delivery gate before Gauntlet III are the constraint.

**Name by name**
- **AVAV** (about $104 to $109): It reported fiscal Q1 2027 on Sept 9 and kept FY27 guidance of $2.125B to $2.225B revenue and $3.02 to $3.34 non-GAAP EPS. Its record funded backlog is $1.5B. Next earnings are likely in early December, but I could not confirm the date. FY26 guidance was cut in March, so there is some history of misses. It is the steadier prime in this group.
- **KTOS:** It hit a 52-week low of $35.71 on Nov 4, then reported Nov 5.
  - Q3 revenue was $471.8M (+35.7%, 23% organic), with a record $2.65B backlog.
