  - It got a Valkyrie low-rate production contract, with Airbus. Free cash flow was -$29M and it does not expect positive cash flow until 2029.
  - It rose 13.8% on Nov 9 to $37.69. It is down about 53% over the past year.
  - It is the least hurt today. I found no company-specific negative news.
- **ONDS** (about $4.67 to $4.77, down about 51% year to date):
  - Q3 revenue was $167.5M against $148M expected, almost all from acquisitions.
  - It raised the 2026 revenue target to at least $550M and set a 2027 target of at least $1.1B. Backlog is $835M.
  - GAAP gross margin was 21.8% (adjusted 34.8%) and net loss was $64.7M.
  - It spent about $431M on acquisitions (one source says $325M).
  - Short interest was about 43% of the float on Oct 30.
  - It has a history of heavy equity issuance. A stale prospectus snippet shows a 19M-share offering at $16.45; I could not date it.
  - Squeeze or dilution moves are both plausible.
- **UMAC** (about $10.84 on Nov 16):
  - Q3 revenue was $13.9M (+551% year over year, -17% from Q2), with gross margin of 35.4% and cash of $162M.
  - The net loss was about $25M, mostly non-cash investment losses.
  - Q4 revenue is guided to about $25M, a big step up that has to be delivered.

- **AVEX** (about $13.65 to $18):
  - It IPO'd in April at $20 and doubled in two sessions, but is now far below the IPO price.
  - A lawsuit alleges an undisclosed early lock-up waiver, which led to an 8M-share secondary at $27 whose roughly $208M of proceeds went to Madison Dearborn, not the company. That secondary caused the June drops. The allegations are unproven, and the lead-plaintiff deadline was Oct 20.

The later searches returned mostly repeats, so I stopped. The sources disagree on several prices, noted below.

**The story**
- **Early November drop.** Natera fell 8.5% on Nov 2 with no company news, and its peers fell too (Myriad -7.9%, Guardant about -4.5%) ([Trefis](https://www.trefis.com/stock/ntra/articles/622219/what-just-happened-to-natera-stock/2026-11-03)). That points to a sector de-risking before earnings.

  - CEO Steve Chapman stepped down, and Solomon Moshkevich succeeds him.
  - The stock had traded at about 17x forward sales, against a 5-year average of 8.9x.
- **Natera since then.** The stock is down about 27% over the month to Nov 16. Reported moves on Nov 16 range from -6.4% to -9.6% (about $288–299), and MarketBeat showed about $279 on Nov 17. I found no specific cause for Nov 16. Insiders sold about $365M over 12 months, with no purchases ([GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9202928/natera-inc-ntra-shares-fall-96-what-gf-score-of-77-tells-investors), [Weiss](https://weissratings.com/en/instant-news-alerts/natera-inc-ntra-down-6-4-cut-and-run)).
- **Guardant (Nov 5).** The quarter was strong but the stock fell about 10%, with no stated cause beyond the market wanting more ([StockStory](https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nasdaq/gh/news/earnings/guardant-healths-nasdaqgh-q3-2026-sales-beat-estimates-but-stock-drops-102percent)).
  - Revenue was $361M (+36%), a beat.
  - Guidance rose to $1.36–1.37B, and Shield (its blood-based colon-cancer screening test) volume was 83,000 tests, more than triple last year.
  - Free cash flow was -$37M for the quarter.
  - Spending plans were reportedly raised for the third time. I could not confirm the new full-year cash-burn range.
  - Cash was about $1.1B.
  - A convertible notes offering of about $500–550M settled around Nov 16. Reports differ on the size.

  - Management targets company-wide cash-flow breakeven by the end of 2027.

  - Revenue was $411.5M (+23%), with a first adjusted profit (adjusted EBITDA $25.6M).

  - Analysts raised targets (Cantor $92, BTIG $100), and Jefferies upgraded to Hold.

  - The Personalis acquisition (about $1.5B, mostly stock) is pending. A November 30 shareholder meeting appeared in one source, but I could not confirm it in filings. Personalis can walk away if Tempus shares fall below $46, which looks far off.
- **Adaptive (Nov 4).** Adaptive has the most mixed picture ([Adaptive release](https://investors.adaptivebiotech.com/news-releases/news-release-details/adaptive-biotechnologies-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial), [Yahoo call highlights](https://finance.yahoo.com/healthcare/articles/adaptive-biotechnologies-corp-adpt-q3-071447835.html)).

**IJR/IWM, 12:10 PM CT Tuesday 2026-11-17: the quality-over-junk spread is the story, and the ratio is already stretched**

I found no source that covers the IJR/IWM ratio itself or today's session. Everything below is context from sources, and several of them conflict. My searching stopped turning up new material, but two fetches failed (CNN with a 451 error, ETF.com with a 403).

**What the ratio is**
- IJR holds the S&P SmallCap 600, which requires positive GAAP earnings (most recent quarter plus trailing four quarters) at entry. IWM holds the Russell 2000, which is sorted by size only.
- About 40% of Russell 2000 companies lose money, versus roughly 20% of the S&P 600 ([Schwab](https://www.schwab.com/learn/story/sp-600-often-overlooked-small-cap-index), [WisdomTree](https://www.wisdomtree.com/us/insights/blog/when-small-cap-junk-leads)).
- IJR/IWM is therefore close to a bet on quality against junk within small caps. It rises when rates climb and risk is shunned, and it falls in speculative rallies.

**Backdrop (late 2025 into 2026)**
- Junk led in 2025. The Russell 2000 rose about 42% from April to October 2025, driven by money-losing names in quantum, crypto, AI, mining and biotech. Quality small caps had one of their worst relative stretches in 30 years ([WisdomTree, Oct 8, 2026](https://www.wisdomtree.com/us/insights/blog/when-small-cap-junk-leads)).
- In 2026 the screen paid off. SPSM (the S&P 600 fund, a close proxy for IJR) was up 23.6% year to date against 21.2% for IWM as of Aug 6 ([24/7 Wall St](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/08/08/forget-iwm-the-small-cap-fund-that-screens-out-money-losers-charges-84-less-and-its-winning-by-2-5-points/)).
- Since the mid-August high, unprofitable small caps are down 15.2% and profitable ones down 6.0% ([HB Wealth](https://hbwealth.com/insights/small-cap-correction-what-are-the-drivers-where-are-the-opportunities/)). That is a single source, but it matches the ratio's run-up.
- Over the long run, the S&P 600 beat the Russell 2000 in 94% of rolling five-year periods ([Morningstar, via search summary](https://www.morningstar.com/funds/4-quality-small-cap-funds-long-term-investors)).

**Macro regime this week**
- The Fed is hiking. A September hike was cited, and a December 8-9 hike is described as priced in or near it, with 78% to 97% quoted. Those figures are inconsistent across sources.
- The 10-year yield is about 5.1%, and the 2-year had its biggest weekly jump in two years after a hot October CPI ([Investrade](https://investrade.com/market-review-november-16-2026/)).
- About 45% of small-cap debt is floating-rate, a figure attributed to Neuberger Berman via a secondary source. That hurts leveraged and unprofitable names most.
- Monday Nov 16: the S&P 500 fell 1.9%, the Nasdaq 2.5% and the Russell 2000 1.7% to about 2,742. The selloff was led by AI and semiconductor names, and the VIX spiked above 24 ([Investrade](https://investrade.com/market-review-november-16-2026/), [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/us-stocks-lower-at-close-of-trade-dow-jones-industrial-average-down-141-5030993)). One source claims Nvidia's CEO resigned, which I did not corroborate.
- The Russell 2000 fell 4.45% in one session on Nov 5 and rebounded Nov 6 ([Beinsure](https://beinsure.com/news/russell-2000-index-forecast-us-small-cap-stocks-rebound/)). That fits the ratio's recent volatility, 1.4 times the prior norm.

**Catalysts inside your 1 to 10 session window**
- FOMC minutes are due Wednesday Nov 18.
- Nvidia earnings are due either Tuesday night or Wednesday after the close. Sources disagree, and most calendars say Wednesday.
- The Anthropic IPO is expected to price Nov 18 and trade Nov 19. This is from one source, and it could pull money out of existing AI allocations.
- Retail sales are due this week, and November jobs and CPI come later. Treat the PPI date as unverified.
- The Russell reconstitution is the first December one in over 30 years. It completes after the close on Dec 11, using Oct 30 rankings. Preliminary lists update Nov 20, Nov 27 and Dec 4 ([Poland Insight, citing FTSE Russell](https://polandinsight.com/russell-2000-december-reconstitution-46631/)). Q3 had a record 27 IPO additions to the Russell 2000. IWM may see turnover flows, but I found no estimates.
- APEC trade headlines may hit this week; the Trump-Xi meeting and the temporary trade truce extension are the swing factors.

**Read for the journal**
- Direction of the story: the move is persistent and rate-driven, not random. Hawkish data, higher yields and risk-off days favor IJR over IWM. A dovish surprise, a soft CPI, a squeeze in speculative names or a risk-on bounce would reverse it fast.
- Today's tape: IWM is down about 1.0% while IJR/IWM is up 0.2%. That fits a risk-off day where junk lags.
- Stretch: at +2.0 standard deviations, a 20-day high, and volatility 1.4 times normal, a snap-back is plausible. The catalysts above cut both ways. A sharp rebound in junk after a heavy Monday selloff, or a soft print, is the main mean-reversion risk.
- Tradeability: IWM has about 30 million shares of average daily volume, against about 4.7 million for IJR. Both ETFs are liquid enough for this purpose.
- Source quality: a lot of the commentary is fund marketing (SPSM, EES) or aggregator text. The yield levels, the hike probabilities and the Nvidia timing vary between sources.

**Bottom line.** SPY is falling with the index, not on its own news. Several catalysts sit inside the one-to-ten-session window. The tape is a rate-driven valuation reset that is being pushed along by AI and tech stress.

1. **Fed hikes are coming.**

It's priced at $70 to $78 per share, with a valuation of up to $1.4T and about $90B raised at the top of the range. **CMC research brief, as of 12:10 PM CT Tue 2026-11-17**

**Bottom line:** I found no company-specific negative catalyst for the drop. The fundamentals are solid and the stock is weak anyway. That fits a sector and multiple-compression drift, not a thesis break. The 8-K and the dated news items I found show no news since the Nov 10 CFO announcement. The web is thin on live-session catalysts, so there may be intraday items I couldn't see.

**What the company reported (fiscal Q4, quarter ended Aug 31, reported Oct 15)**
- Adjusted EPS was $2.09 against a consensus of about $1.96–1.97. Revenue was $2.66B (+25.7%) against about $2.57B expected.
- Core EBITDA rose 35% to $393.7M, a 14.8% margin. The fiscal-year figure was $1.36B, up from $837M.
- North America Steel adjusted EBITDA was $317.5M, with metal margin of $652/ton (+$84 year over year, +$42 from Q3). Merchant bar shipments rose 27.5% on the expanded Arizona 2 mill. Rebar volume was roughly flat to down (one source says -6.8%).
- Construction Solutions (CSG, the downstream and precast business) sales rose 94.5% on acquisitions. Backlog is near record, with downstream backlog +15.5% year over year.
- Fiscal 2027 outlook: management expects "another strong year." It targets about $100M of added run-rate EBITDA from its TAG initiatives and expects "structurally higher free cash flow."
- Buyback: the board added $600M in August. About $702M remains, but Q4 repurchases were only $26.7M. The company said it would speed up buybacks.
- The stock was about $65.34 right after the report. Today's 59.27 is roughly 9% below that.

**Negatives, most of which were already known at the report**
- The Q1 fiscal 2027 guide is soft. North America Steel EBITDA is expected to be roughly flat sequentially, with better pricing offset by higher scrap, startup costs and a seasonal dip in shipments. CSG is expected to decline on seasonality. Europe is expected to grow.
- Precast EBITDA ($57M) missed management's own expectations because of residential weakness and weak Southeast shipments.
- An unplanned outage at the Galvabar line (a coated-rebar line) hurt shipments. The second line is due later in calendar 2026.
- Europe Steel adjusted EBITDA fell to $15.6M from $39.1M, mostly because last year's quarter included a $30.7M CO2 credit.
- Debt rose to $3.31B from $1.31B to fund $2.52B of acquisitions, and interest expense tripled to $37.4M. Net leverage is 1.9x.
- Risk factors list Section 232 tariffs and quotas, and the Pacific Steel litigation.

**Analysts**
- Price targets were mostly trimmed after the report. BMO cut to $73 (market perform) and Morgan Stanley to $84 (overweight) on Oct 19. Goldman has a buy at $85. Barclays raised to $77 (equal weight) around Nov 12–13.
- Consensus is Moderate Buy: 10 buy, 4 hold, 1 sell, average target about $78.7. That is about 33% above the current price.
- Wall Street Zen cut to hold on Oct 17.
- An Investing.com piece from Nov 4 cited a pessimistic Zacks Research forecast on Nov 2 and short interest up about 5%.

**Management change**
- On Nov 10 CMC announced that CFO Paul Lawrence will retire.
- Kenji Hashimoto joins Nov 16 as deputy CFO and is expected to become CFO Jan 15, 2027. Lawrence stays on as advisor through June 30, 2027.
- His background is Global Infrastructure Partners, Amazon and American Airlines.

- Tariff headlines move the group. Examples are the August report of a US–Canada deal halving the Canadian steel tariff to 25% and the April derivative-tariff changes. CMC is largely a domestic rebar maker and tends to be less exposed than flat-rolled names.
- The data-center and semiconductor build-out is a key demand narrative for CMC. An AI-capex scare hits that narrative.

**Payroll and HR software (ADP, PAYX, PAYC, PCTY, WDAY): research as of 12:10 PM CT, Tue 2026-11-17**

**Bottom line:** The basket's relative strength looks like a rotation story, not a payroll-specific improvement. Software has been falling on AI seat-compression fears, and today's drop is being tied to the Anthropic IPO. Payroll names with float income and recent beats have held up better, while the pure seat-priced name, WDAY, is getting hit hardest. The next few sessions carry a binary event, the Anthropic pricing on Nov 18. WDAY earnings on Nov 24 fall inside a 1 to 10 session window. I found no news today specific to any of the five except WDAY's move.

**Market backdrop**
- IGV was down about 3.4% to 3.7% today, its fifth daily drop of 3% or more since Oct 16 (Benzinga, CNBC).
- Salesforce fell about 9% and ServiceNow about 7% with no company news. HubSpot fell about 7% and Workday about 5%.
- Yahoo's explanation is that funds are selling seat-priced software to make room for Anthropic's roughly $61-64B IPO, which is expected to price Nov 18 and trade Nov 19. Yahoo itself says this is the author's interpretation, not a confirmed cause.
- The underlying fear is that AI agents shrink seat counts. RBC's Rishi Jaluria said the AI companies "are going to try to destroy Salesforce entirely."
- Yahoo cites a precedent from June: IGV fell 7% around the SpaceX listing while the Nasdaq 100 rose 3%. That implies a possible bounce after the pricing.
- A separate item says new US AI chip export restrictions are pressuring tech broadly.
- This explains the screen: the basket's spread against IGV is stretched because IGV is collapsing, not because these five are rallying.
- Today's declines (WDAY -5.0%, ADP -1.4%) show the basket is still falling in absolute terms.

**Company by company**

- **ADP**
  - It reported fiscal Q1 2027 on Oct 28 and raised its outlook.
  - Revenue was up 6% to $5.5B, adjusted EPS up 13% to $2.82, and adjusted EBIT margin 26.8%, up 130 bps.
  - US pays per control rose 2%, and the fiscal 2027 forecast went to about 1% from 0% to 1%.
  - EPS growth guidance is now 10% to 12% (was 9% to 11%), and revenue growth about 6%.
  - It earned $329M on client fund interest, up 15% year over year. That float income is sensitive to rates.
  - It is the steadiest and lowest-beta name, which fits it being the best performer today at -1.4%.

- **Paychex**
  - Fiscal Q1 on Sep 23 had revenue up about 6% to $1.63B and adjusted EPS of $1.34, in line.
  - Guidance was unchanged at 5% to 6% revenue growth, though PEO growth was raised.
  - The stock fell roughly 7% to 9% on the report. Sources disagree on the exact figure.
  - Q2 revenue growth is guided to about 4%. The dividend takes about 90% of net income.
  - It was $115.58 on Nov 13, down about 8% over the past year, and Morningstar calls it fully valued.
  - The next earnings report is around December, and I did not confirm the date.

- **Paycom**
  - It reported Q3 on Nov 4 and beat. Revenue was $543.8M, up 10.2%, and non-GAAP EPS was $3.37 against about $2.80 expected. It raised the 2026 revenue guide to about $2.213B to $2.218B.
  - The stock still fell 4.8% to 6.8% after the report. BTIG downgraded it to neutral on valuation, and Citi cut its target.
  - The stock had run hard, at about $274 on Oct 23 and $254.90 after the report.
  - A beat followed by a selloff on valuation shows it is crowded, and it is the name most at risk if the relative-strength trade unwinds.

- **Paylocity**
  - It reported fiscal Q1 on Nov 5 and beat. Revenue was $451.7M, up 10.7%, and adjusted EPS was $2.09 against $1.93 expected.
  - It raised fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $1.910B to $1.925B, which is about 8% growth and a deceleration from Q1's roughly 11%.
  - The stock hit new 52-week highs on Nov 6 (intraday $178.70) and again on Nov 16.
  - Analysts raised targets (BTIG $210, Truist $200, Citizens JMP $200, Barclays $176), but the consensus average of about $177 is roughly at the price.
  - It is the momentum leader, so it is extended and a candidate for a sharp pullback if software keeps selling off.

- **Workday**
  - The stock is down about 5% today. One report says it closed at $185.25, but that is unreliable because the session is still open.
  - The range is about $110 to $237. It was down about 43% year to date in May, so it is rebounding from deep lows.
  - It reports Q3 fiscal 2027 on Nov 24 after the close. Consensus is roughly $2.69B revenue, with non-GAAP EPS estimates ranging from $2.45 to $2.75 depending on source.
  - Subscription growth was 13.9% last quarter, and the stock needs that to hold up.
  - It has beaten EPS in 7 of the last 8 quarters.
  - Workday said at its Analyst Day that AI products are approaching $600M ARR, and Sana is nearing $100M.
  - It has a large buyback ($4B authorization) and Elliott as an activist holder (a $2B stake disclosed in Sep 2025).
  - The consensus rating is Hold, and the average target of about $202 is above the current price.
  - Workday is the clearest seat-compression casualty, because HR seats are exposed to white-collar headcount cuts. It is the highest-beta name to the Anthropic news and the only one with an earnings date inside the window.

**Cross-cutting themes**
- **Labor market:** The October jobs report was reportedly strong (165,000 against 65,000 expected, though sources differ on consensus). That helps pays per control for ADP and PAYX. Falling rates would reduce float income.
- **AI as threat versus tool:** Payroll processors are seen as less seat-exposed than WDAY or CRM. Paychex says its AI cuts manual processing by about 20%.
- **Deceleration:** Guides are modest (ADP revenue about 6%, PAYX 5% to 6%, PCTY about 8%, PAYC about 8%), so valuations rely on stability, not growth.

**Trade read for 1 to 10 sessions**
- The basket's spread against IGV is hostage to the Anthropic pricing and the software tape.
- If IGV bounces after Nov 18 to 19, as in the June precedent, the spread likely mean-reverts. It is already 2.1 standard deviations stretched, so it is a poor chase.
- Of the five, PCTY and PAYC are the most extended, and WDAY is the most event-exposed. ADP and PAYX are lower-beta.
- Conflicts to keep in mind: reaction sizes for PAYX and PAYC differ by source, the WDAY earnings-date estimate varies (Nov 24 is most credible, TipRanks says Dec 1), and I could not check live prices for any of the five. I also did not confirm the Anthropic pricing date beyond "expected Nov 18".

I found no news catalyst for today's move. The basket is stretched up on strong fundamentals and a rates backdrop that has been unstable. Several search summaries conflicted, and the Home Depot figures come from a search snippet, so verify those before relying on them.

**The story**
- **Earnings were strong and every name raised guidance.** The reports came out between Oct 29 and Nov 5, so they are 12 to 19 days old.
  - SPG (Nov 5):
    - Real estate FFO of $3.37 a share, up 4.7%.
    - Full-year guidance raised $0.10 to $13.30–$13.40.
    - Occupancy 96.5%, the highest since 2016.
    - Quarterly dividend $2.30, up $0.10.
    - University Village (Seattle) acquisition is set to close in Q4.
  - KIM (Oct 29):
    - FFO of $0.47, up 6.8%.
    - Guidance raised to $1.84–$1.86.
    - Occupancy 96.6%, a record.
    - Same-property NOI growth of 4.9%.
    - Bought back $150M of stock at about $23.80.
    - Management said the tenant watch list is the smallest its CFO has seen.
  - REG (Nov 5):
    - Core operating earnings of $1.18, up 8.3%.
    - Same-property NOI up 5.1%.
    - Leased rate 97.0%, a company high.
    - Dividend raised 6% to $0.80.
    - Guidance raised.
  - FRT (Oct 30):
    - Core FFO of $1.87, up 5.6%.
    - Guidance raised to $7.54–$7.58.
    - Bought The Summit in Birmingham, Alabama, for $508M (announced Oct 1).
    - Repurchased about 870,000 shares.
  - O (early Nov):
    - AFFO of $1.12, up 3.7%.
    - Guidance raised to $4.45–$4.46.
    - Credit-loss assumption cut to about 30 basis points.
    - Invested $2.6B in the quarter, about 42% of it in Europe.
    - Raised its monthly dividend again, the 137th raise since 1994.
- **Stocks tied to lower yields.** Realty Income's financing cost (about 5% against a 6.8% initial cash yield) leaves it the most rate-sensitive of the five and the least tied to US retail.
- **Consumer data is supportive.**
  - Simon reported October traffic up in the mid-3% range and comparable sales up 4.9%.
  - US October retail sales rose 0.2%, with the ex-gasoline-and-autos figure at 0.6% against 0.4% expected.
  - Home Depot's comparable sales were up 2.2%, against a 1.5% consensus that one analyst had raised to 2.5%.

**Risks and headwinds**
- **Rates are the main risk.**
  - The 10-year is about 5.13% and the 30-year about 5.47% today.
  - CME FedWatch shows roughly a 95% chance of a December hike. The St. Louis Fed's Musalem said the Fed may need four more.
  - Strong consumer data supports the case for higher rates.
  - FOMC minutes come out Wednesday, and Waller and Williams speak today.
  - The REIT index fell 5.7% in September on rates. XLRE rose about 1.9% around Nov 7 as yields dropped after the midterms.
- **2027 guidance is cooler.**
  - SPG flagged about a $0.30 per-share interest-expense headwind, with $2B of debt maturing in 2027.
  - REG guided mid-3% same-property NOI growth for 2027. It expects refinancing to cut long-term earnings growth by 150 to 200 basis points, and bad debt to rise from about 25 to about 50 basis points.
  - KIM and FRT have not yet given 2027 outlooks.
- **Occupancy gains are nearly maxed out.** REG sees only 40 to 50 basis points of upside left. Rent growth and expense control have to carry the rest.
- **Competition in grocery.** Analysts asked REG about Kroger's store expansion and Albertsons' real estate review.
- **Analysts.**
  - Analysts trimmed KIM price targets in October, though the consensus is still Buy at about $25.8.
  - O's consensus is Hold, with an average target of about $72. Scotiabank downgraded it in September.
  - I found no dated rating changes in November for any of the five.

**Catalysts in the 1 to 10 session window**
- Target reports Wed Nov 18, and Walmart and Ross report Thu Nov 19 (Lowe's date unconfirmed).
- FOMC minutes are Wednesday.
- Rate-hike odds and yield moves are the dominant driver, and a December FOMC hike would land in the days after the window.
- I found no confirmed ex-dividend dates in the window. Realty Income pays monthly, so it likely has one. I could not verify KIM's date of December 4.

**XBI research, Tuesday 2026-11-17, about 12:10 PM CT**

**Bottom line:** The weakness looks macro and sentiment driven, not tied to a single biotech event. The main drivers are rising long yields and a risk-off day on Monday (11/16). A wave of disappointing trial readouts since August also weighs. XBI sits right on a widely watched chart level near $143, which is the 200-day. I found no fresh biotech-specific shock today. Sources conflict on the size of Monday's drop, and I couldn't get any intraday news for today.

**How XBI got here**
- XBI peaked near $170 in August, more than doubling in a year (52-week range $113.06 to $169.89).
- BioPharma Dive (Oct 9) blamed the pullback on disappointing trial readouts, rising rates, midterm-election worries and a slowdown in public-company takeovers. About half of surveyed investors still expect a rebound before year-end.
- One chart analyst (Nov 14) ties the decline to the 10-year Treasury yield:
  - It went from 4.62% in late August to 5.36% in early October, and is now back above 5.15%.
  - Over that stretch XBI fell from about $180 to about $143, as the analyst puts it.
  - A sustained break above 5.36% could push XBI below $143.
- XBI was about $155 on Nov 10 and fell 1.1% in the week of Nov 9 (BowTiedBiotech). It is still up about 24% year to date.

**Monday 11/16 and today**
- Monday was a broad risk-off day:
  - The S&P 500 fell 1.92%, the Nasdaq 2.49% and the VIX spiked to about 24.
  - Chips led the drop. Nvidia's CEO resigned on Nov 12 and a new Commerce rule restricts remote access to advanced chips. The Empire State factory index also came in weak.
  - Consumer staples were the only S&P 500 sector that rose.
- XBI closed Monday at $145.88, down about 3.1% according to Tickeron. Other sources say 1% to 2.3%, so treat the size as uncertain.
- Today (per StockAnalysis, 1:10 PM ET): XBI was $145.33, down 0.38%, with a range of $143.24 to $147.72. It opened at $147.07 and sold off to the low of the range.
- Nvidia reports after the close tonight (about 4:20 PM ET), which could swing risk appetite tomorrow. Retail sales and industrial production came out this morning, but I found no coverage of them.
- Biotech news on Monday was mixed:
  - Summit's FDA rejection of ivonescimab: -16.5%. The FDA said overall survival was not significantly improved.
  - Aclaris missed in a Phase 2 atopic dermatitis trial: -8%.
  - CG Oncology had a positive Phase 3 bladder cancer result: +14%.
  - Lexeo had positive early gene therapy data: +12.5%.
- Summit is not a major XBI holding. XBI is equal-weighted, so no single name moves it much. Its top holding is only 2.46%, and the top 10 together are 18.7% (Moderna, Biogen, Amgen, Regeneron, AbbVie and others).

**Technical picture from other analysts**
- Tickeron lists the bearish signals:
  - XBI went below its 50-day on Nov 12.
  - The 10-day crossed below the 50-day the same day.
  - MACD turned negative on Nov 13.
  - Its page dates are inconsistent, so treat it as low quality.
- The Nov 14 chart analysis sees a possible head-and-shoulders pattern with a neckline at $143:
  - A break would target about $118 (the March low).
  - Resistance is $170 (April peak) and about $180 (prior high).
  - The 200-day at 143.10 coincides with that neckline, so $143 is a key level. A clean break below it would open the downside.
- Elliott-wave and bullish views call the decline corrective. State Street and Fidelity analysts stay constructive.

**Supportive factors**
- Biotech M&A is on pace for its best year since before Covid, about $106B so far in 2026. Recent deals include Lilly/Merida (up to $2.9B), Biogen/RayThera (up to $1B), GSK/Nuvalent ($10.6B, month unconfirmed) and Merck KGaA/Silence (about $1.3B). A Nov 13 roundup called last week quiet for full buyouts.
- The IPO window is reopening (Windward Bio raised $175M).
- Big pharma is near record highs on defensive rotation.
- Valuation is moderate: forward P/E 18.3, beta 0.86.

**Catalysts in the 1 to 10 session window**
- **Nov 17 (today):**
  - Nvidia earnings after the close.
  - Acadia's Phase 2 Alzheimer's psychosis data: the 60 mg dose narrowly missed the main goal, and Phase 3 continues at the higher dose.
  - Beren's FDA date for adrabetadex.
  - CTAD Alzheimer's data from Eisai/Biogen and Roche, and the end of ObesityWeek.
- **Nov 18:** Innate Pharma data and investor event.
- **Nov 22 (a Sunday):** FDA dates for Capricor (deramiocel in Duchenne) and Savara (molgramostim). A decision could come Friday or Monday.
- **November, no date:** Sellas Phase 3 topline.
- **Other:** Moderna may file its cancer vaccine, and the Fed December meeting is a rate risk. I found no Fed odds for 2026.

**Policy backdrop (background only, nothing dated November)**
- Pharma tariffs under Section 232 are in effect, with 0% for firms that have most-favored-nation pricing and onshoring deals.
- FDA leadership has been turbulent (Prasad's tenure, Pazdur's departure).

**Caveats**
- Some sources are inconsistent. A Stocktwits piece said XBI -1% while SPY +3% for the week, and its Nov 16 market numbers disagree with other sources.
- The Tickeron page is internally contradictory.
- Several search results were stale.
